The example owns their execution composition: fresh inner runs, isolated hidden test workspaces, captured evidence, and only token/spend/elapsed roll-up. Evaluator configuration identity covers suite digest, split, worker/model, inner budget, timeouts, environment, and scoring version.

Held-out comparison accepts only two seed-only Greedy(max_trials=0) runs and fails closed on any changed control or immutable harness declaration. Export is harness-specific rather than a speculative capability on every codec: it stages beside the destination, reconstructs and verifies the artifact digest, then atomically swaps only absent or valid prior harness exports.

The fixture TFD remains user code. The opt-in driver under experiments/08_harness_evolution_live/ imports one official SDK directly and adds no package dependency. Its first authorized result is retained as an unchanged tie after both proposal calls failed strict output-schema validation. That capture remains unchanged. Later authorized runs reached native mutation decoding and the trusted successor boundary in closed PR #162; they are historical closure evidence, not a broader shipped live-provider surface.

docs.title: Milestone 8.7: audited prior-candidate source inspection
docs.text: Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). This independent post-M8 program is tracked by

docs.title: 150 and does not widen the M8.6 closure gate or M9.5. It first proves value
docs.text:
through existing durable evidence, then locks a Git-neutral source-access manifest before adding audited path reads, canonical source diffs, and an optional disposable read-only Git projection.

The capability remains same-task, same-run, strictly prior, occurrence-based, and bounded by ExperienceGrant. Every returned source observation is audited and replayed from committed facts. Git metadata stays outside artifacts and durable identity; no coordinator branch depends on source artifacts or their presentation adapter.

docs.title: M8.7.2 — contract and serialization
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). This stage extended the port and durable contract without adding methods to AuditedExperienceReader; M8.7.3 implements listing and reads, and M8.7.4 implements diffing:

class ExperienceReader(Protocol):
    def list_source_paths(
        self, artifact_ref, *, as_of=None, limit=None
    ) -> SourcePathListing: ...

    def read_source(
        self, artifact_ref, *, paths, as_of=None
    ) -> SourceRead: ...

    def diff_source(
        self,
        older_artifact_ref,
        newer_artifact_ref,
        *,
        paths=(),
        as_of=None,
    ) -> SourceDiff: ...

domain/experience_access.py adds the operation names and the canonically omitted ExperienceRequest.paths default. Legacy requests and containing audit events therefore retain exact schema-v3 bytes. Only a non-tuple or non-string path is rejected before auditing; semantic path, kind, limit, and logical-time errors remain opaque denials. At this stage application/experience_operations.py explicitly denied all three source operations before legacy comparison dispatch.

domain/source_access.py owns SourcePathListing, SourceFile, SourceRead, SourceDiffEntry, and SourceDiff. Results carry verified digests, complete ordered entries, canonical text, truncation, and cumulative ExperienceUsage. Listing order is normalized lexicographic order; reads preserve caller order; paths are normalized and unique. Diff status is added, deleted, or modified under meta-evolve-unified-diff/v1. All records join the closed durable serializer and remain off the root surface.

Capacity resolution first authorizes and proves existence, then reserves one result for listing/read or two for diff, then retains the largest whole-entry prefix fitting record and character ceilings. Missing result capacity is ExperienceBudgetExhausted; a missing read path is atomic ExperienceAccessDenied. Neither consumes protected result, record, or character capacity. Each retained entry is one record and the character delta is exactly len(rendered). Listing uses compact JSON strings; reading uses compact JSON Lines with exactly path and source, stable keys, preserved Unicode, and no trailing newline. M8.7.3 implements resolution plus listing/read rendering; M8.7.4 implements unified diffs and their replay checks.

domain/source_history.py owns SourceHistoryBounds, SourceHistoryEntry, and SourceHistoryManifest. source-history-manifest/v1 requires a non-empty ordered entry tuple whose first artifact is head_ref. Artifact refs are unique while digests may repeat. Artifact, parent, proposal, and evaluation refs have exact kinds and one run; parents remain contained in the manifest. Entries retain logical step and non-empty selection rationale. No source bytes, Git IDs or refs, commits, trees, environment, or layout fields are present.

The later adapter declaration is fixed as:

meta.PatchProposer(
    edit,
    history=meta_evolve.adapters.GitHistoryView(
        max_ancestors=...,
        max_archive_members=...,
        max_chars=...,
    ),
)

GitHistoryView was not implemented in this stage. M8.7.5 now builds its manifest through ordinary audited traversal, listing, and reading, then records one mount fact without charging those bytes twice. Later Git commands are not independently audited. PullAccess remains outer authority and all history bounds are explicit.

M8.7.3 also owns an application-only ExperienceOperationUsage view. It omits zero totals and orders entries by search, open, ancestors, siblings, compare, list_source_paths, read_source, and diff_source. Their dimension-wise sum equals RunExperienceUsage.pull; there is no Git-mount usage category or new durable event.

Historical annotation. M8.7.5 narrowly supersedes the earlier “no new durable event” reservation with one SourceHistoryMounted fact because a truthful pre-execution mount must be replayable. It does not change the locked reader signatures, audit accounting, component/artifact identities, authority rules, or the claim that there is no Git-mount usage category. This final-stage repair is local to M8.7's projection contract and is not permission to reopen other shipped milestones.

docs.title: M8.7.3 — audited source listing and reads
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). A focused source-resolution edge accepts an already-authorized artifact occurrence, loads it through ArtifactStore, revalidates its content digest, and decodes only exact source-tree / utf8-tree-v1 payloads. The host supplies this dependency to AuditedExperienceReader; neither the coordinator nor generic experience graph branches on artifact type.

application/source_operations.py owns listing/read rendering and complete- entry prefix selection. Generic experience_operations.py dispatches those two operations there; M8.7.4 extends the same seam for diff_source. Authorization and tree resolution precede result reservation; every requested read path is proved before either content disclosure or charging. A successful operation consumes one result plus one record per retained entry and exactly the final joined rendering length in characters.

Both operation-ceiling and source result-ceiling exhaustion append the existing durable exhaustion fact with attempted cumulative usage. Event folding checks the result type, target occurrence, logical boundary, deltas, path order, and canonical rendering. Committed reader replay returns that result without live resolution. load_validated_run separately resolves the durable artifact and reproduces digest, selected prefix, file text, rendering, truncation, and usage for reopen, resume, and cross-process reconstruction.

Successful listing/read results add their exact artifact occurrence to the derivation observation ledger. The application view meta_evolve.views.ExperienceOperationUsage supplies canonical, non-zero per-operation totals on RunExperienceUsage.by_operation; their dimension-wise sum is required to equal the unchanged aggregate pull usage.

docs.title: M8.7.4 — canonical audited source diffs
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). The audited reader dispatches diff_source through the existing source-operation seam. It authorizes and resolves the older occurrence before the newer occurrence, then reserves two results atomically. The coordinator, artifact adapters, root surface, Experiment, and schema-v3 serializer require no special case or migration.

The pure application/source_diff.py renderer compares normalized logical lines with a deterministic Myers edit script and deletion-first ties. It owns sorted/filtered changed-path selection, three-line context and six-line hunk merging, JSON file operands, uniform ranges, and final-newline markers. It uses neither the human presentation diff nor difflib, Git, or subprocesses. source_operations.py applies whole-entry record/character prefix bounds and charges two results, one record per retained entry, and exactly the joined rendering length.

Event folding validates both refs and their logical visibility, canonical entry order and self-contained rendering, truncation shape, and cumulative usage. Successful operand refs enter derivation observations in order. Durable loading resolves both artifacts and rebuilds the exact diff, while ordinary reader replay returns the committed result without live artifact access. At this stage M8.7.5 remained the only open M8.7 stage and owned Git history projection.

docs.title: M8.7.5 — authorized read-only Git history
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). adapters/git_history.py owns the adapter declaration and explicit bounds. application/source_history.py owns the canonical audited request prefix, causal/archive selection, complete-tree character bound, and replay reconstruction. SourceHistoryMounted is folded only after that prefix resolves and before ProposalSubmitted; its transition checks trial authority, selected parent, observed version, exact operation prefix, ordering, refs, digests, and manifest equality.

adapters/git_projection.py owns only disposable Git plumbing. It builds blobs, trees, and commits parent-first in an external sidecar, supplies controlled absolute GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, and GIT_INDEX_FILE values through WorkspaceSession, creates deterministic archive refs, disables ambient configuration and executable extension points, freezes the result read-only, and disposes it before workspace capture. PatchProposer proves the callback did not mutate that workspace before applying its one returned TextPatch.

The adapter version and bounds enter configured proposer identity. With history=None, constructor behavior and identity remain byte-for-byte compatible. No generic reader, coordinator, experiment, root-export, or artifact-storage special case is introduced.

docs.title: Milestone 9: policy evolution
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. The dependency is M8.1–M8.5, not #124 or M8.6. The deterministic implementation is examples/research/policy_evolution/.

meta_evolve.mutation owns only the generic MutationApplication result and MutationSurface protocol. Harness keeps compatibility re-exports and all harness-specific values. meta_evolve.policy owns the parallel policy domain: search-policy / policy-manifest-v1, schema-fixed ParentSelection and TrialLimit, one-surface PolicyMutation, portable PolicyEpisode and PolicySuite, captured EpisodeOutcome, aggregate PolicyEvaluation, and strict PolicyComparison. No generic episode/comparison framework was added.

The built-in candidate-policy@1 interpreter is registered with Registry.register_policy(). Its exact policy-manifest payload is frozen into the SearchSpec configuration. Seed selection always expands the original artifact; incumbent selection uses SearchState.incumbent_id; the voluntary trial limit never widens the run budget. Durable-local run and resume paths resolve it through the unchanged registry seam.

The published SearchProgramTests suite covers all four built-in policies. MutationSurfaceTests takes plural (mutation, expected successor) pairs and invalid_mutations, observes successors through an inert canonical-bytes projection rather than the surface's own equality, and runs unchanged against both harness and both policy surfaces.

Nested execution remains user-owned composition around ordinary meta.run() calls. Each outcome retains an inner RunId and storage location. Development may reopen an exact completed run and resume a permitted incomplete durable run; held-out execution creates a fresh empty namespace. Aggregation is recomputed from all outcomes, becomes non-rankable on any failed, incomplete, or missing episode, and rolls up only token, monetary-spend, and elapsed usage.

Separate outer Greedy(max_trials=0) runs capture held-out baseline and candidate evaluations. meta.compare_policies() requires equality of every external control and immutable surface declaration; only the two schema-owned surface values may differ. It returns improvement, tie, regression, or unrankable and reports strict promotion eligibility without promoting.

docs.title: Milestone 9.5: advanced search
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 17, 2026). M9.5.1 ships shared archive compatibility, M9.5.2 ships replayable specialist retention, M9.5.3 ships replayable tree search, and M9.5.4 ships the unified deterministic five-policy comparison. ArchiveUpdate.member_ids remains the complete ordered result, while the single-removal compatibility field is None for zero or multiple removals. This changes validation only: the durable schema, coordinator, commitment, inspection, recovery, and existing Population decisions remain unchanged.

meta_evolve.policies.Specialists now ships as specialists@1; it is not a root export. Its exact ordered metrics and trial limit are durable configuration, and the built-in registry reconstructs the bound preset. Committed successful evaluations reconstruct strict per-metric winners and ordered membership without a cache. Metric-uniform selection uses selection, proposal randomness uses trial, and archive membership remains authoritative for zero-, one-, or multiple-removal transitions. This is GEPA-style per-key retention, not Pareto ranking.

meta_evolve.policies.TreeSearch now ships as tree-search@1; it is not a root export. Its max_trials and exploration are durable configuration, and the built-in registry reconstructs the bound preset. A private immutable fold reconstructs one node per materialized artifact occurrence, visit counts, subtree Q values, the normalization range, and widening eligibility entirely from committed trial and evaluation facts. Selection widens a node with a new child while child_count < ceil(sqrt(node_visits)), otherwise it descends by normalized best-descendant UCT, breaking exact ties by ascending artifact occurrence ID. Only trial randomness is recorded.

examples/learn/policy_comparison/advanced_search.py ships the unified comparison. BestOfN, Greedy, Population, Specialists, and TreeSearch run on the same specialist-retention and delayed-reward fixtures under identical task, seed, proposer, evaluator, root randomness, budget, and explicit trial limit, with equality verified pairwise through the existing Run.compare() gate. The specialist fixture shows Specialists retaining an aggregate-weak per-case winner that capacity-matched Population evicts, reaching the aggregate winner that equal-budget BestOfN cannot. The delayed-reward fixture shows Greedy plateauing on the immediately attractive branch while TreeSearch revisits the weaker delayed branch and reaches its descendant. Every result reports primary score, winning lineage and depth, every selected parent, evaluation and failure counts, archive behavior, and exact usage. No shared selector protocol, private policy engine, or coordinator branch is created in advance.

docs.title: Milestone 10: local author API and inspection experience
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 14, 2026; #149). This milestone does not depend on M8.6 or M9.5. Its nine one-PR stages are #151 (M10.0), #152 (M10.1), #165 (M10.2), #164 (M10.3), #153 (M10.4), #154 (M10.5), #166 (M10.6), #156 (M10.7), and #157 (M10.8).

The subordinate M10.0 design record owns the six journeys, vocabulary, measurements, and alternatives. Technical staging is:

  • Shipped — M10.1: the frozen declaration value lives in application/experiment.py without moving storage, mode, or the narrowing budget out of run(). Keyword calls lower to the same declaration. CLI parsing stays in cli.py; dictionary factories remain supported through 1.x with a DeprecationWarning beside the typed alternative.
  • Shipped — M10.2: application/improvement.py implements improve() in the application callable boundary. It lowers exactly through Task(evaluator=...), Experiment, Greedy(max_trials=trials), and local run(..., storage=...); it adds no second coordinator path and no durable-local claim.
  • Shipped — M10.3: policies/functional.py implements the curated @meta.search adapter and shares one private incumbent decision lowerer with Greedy. The callback never receives kernel state; immutable serializable configuration flows into SearchSpec identity, and DecisionDescription derives from the decorated name and cleaned docstring. Population actions remain on the full extension protocol.
  • Shipped — M10.4: application/inspection.py owns the immutable aggregate read model, while a shared application/views.py builder keeps artifact, evidence, trial-state, and lineage construction single-sourced. One Run.inspect() call performs exactly one validated replay.
  • Shipped — M10.5: Storage.read_only() wires dedicated read-only artifact, blob, event, and unit-of-work implementations. adapters/sqlite/ opens with mode=ro, enables query_only, validates without DDL or migration, and reads the maximum committed event sequence in a fresh deferred transaction. It does not use immutable=1, so one handle observes later WAL commits.
  • Shipped — M10.6: application/session.py owns the small public lifecycle, while one preparation boundary reconstructs fresh and resumed coordinators. run() and resume() exhaust Session; authority and budget are fixed at start, and recovery completes committed work rather than accepting injected decisions.
  • Shipped — M10.7: browser/reader.py owns a single-threaded read-only handle, exact-version catalog cards, and separate 32-entry inspection and comparison LRUs. browser/app.py supplies escaped server-rendered routes, same-origin polling, safe failure translation, and security headers over root-exported APIs only. cli.py conditionally delegates ui to a fixed loopback, one-worker Uvicorn lifecycle.
  • Shipped — M10.8: presentation/ owns dependency-free inert records, exact kind/representation dispatch, deterministic preview bounds, semantic direct-parent diffs, and canonical-payload-v1 bytes. ArtifactView retains its frozen payload without changing decoded value, equality, or repr semantics. Browser artifact/diff/raw routes resolve occurrences within one exact inspection snapshot; templates remain escaped, and the CLI's optional module contributes only its registry for custom-codec reconstruction. Notebook HTML is owned by the post-M10 presentation follow-up below.

The dependency order is M10.0 → (M10.1, M10.3, M10.4, M10.5), M10.1 → M10.2, M10.1 + M10.4 → M10.6, M10.4 + M10.5 → M10.7, and M10.7 → M10.8.

Core installation remains dependency-free. M10.7–M10.8 form the shipped bounded exception to the general dashboard prohibition, and only after M10.4 and M10.5 stabilize the public inspection, query, read-only storage, and version contracts. Its optional meta_evolve.browser package imports those public surfaces only—never Session, run, resume, proposers, evaluators, internal projections, or persistence implementations. cli.py conditionally imports it for the UI command. It binds to loopback, remains read-only, and exposes no operational, mutable, remote, collaboration, or distributed controls.

The browser extra contains Starlette, Jinja, and Uvicorn: Starlette supplies tested routing and lifecycle, Jinja supplies escaped templates, and Uvicorn supplies server operation without bespoke web infrastructure. They do not enter core dependencies. Presentation itself remains dependency-free.

docs.title: Post-M10 presentation follow-up
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. This future slice owns notebook HTML representations over M10.8's shipped inert records and browser screenshot or visual-regression automation. The safe presentation boundary is a dependency, not permission to claim notebook rendering today. This work is outside the M10 closure gate and requires a separate implementation and acceptance gate.

docs.title: Milestone 11: trusted distribution
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped. Tracked by #10.

Only after local semantics are stable:

  • add WorkAttempt and durable lease acquisition, renewal, expiration, cancellation, and completion;
  • retain one logical Trial across delivery retries;
  • introduce trusted worker identities and capability matching;
  • add atomic budget reservation and settlement;
  • make idempotent result submission explicit;
  • define consistency requirements per state type;
  • load-test simulated populations before paid agent fleets.

The canonical reservation is examples/research/trusted_workers/.

Worker liveness and queue estimates are ephemeral. Accepted outcomes, evaluations, budgets, and promotion decisions are durable. Out-of-order wall-clock completion must not alter logical random choices or reveal future experience.

docs.title: Milestone 12: contributed and federated network
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped. Tracked by #11 and dependent on M11.

Add signed manifests, scoped contributor identities, task-specific trust policies, visibility, licensing, embargoes, attribution, retraction, disputes, and reputation. Exchange policy-filtered subgraphs rather than assuming universal access.

References may be redacted, tombstoned, or inaccessible while preserving enough metadata to maintain causal structure. Untrusted execution, evaluator collusion, poisoning, sybil attacks, reward hacking, and correlated replication remain separate threats with separate controls.

The canonical reservation is examples/research/federated_exchange/.

docs.title: Interface staging
docs.text: Capability First implementation Later implementation Proposer local callable SDK agent, human workflow, composite harness Evaluator pure callable isolated grader, simulator, proof checker Artifact store in-memory payloads content-addressed filesystem or object store Event store in-memory list SQLite, then durable service Search greedy and best-of-N populations, Pareto, islands, learned allocation Experience no memory exact graph traversal, then measured semantic retrieval Workspace absent directory copy, Git tree/worktree, remote volume Sandbox absent development subprocess, container, hardened remote sandbox Identity absent or local stub trusted worker, then signed contributor identity

docs.title: What not to build first
docs.text:
• every module in the destination package tree;
  • a custom graph or vector database;
  • a peer-to-peer protocol or token economy;
  • a thousand-agent deployment;
  • mutable, operational, or remote dashboards, and any browser before stable public event and query contracts;
  • universal agent communication;
  • learned scheduling without strong baselines;
  • unrestricted self-modification;
  • a template DSL when local closures and typed durable manifests suffice;
  • scientific-discovery claims without domain evidence and replication.

docs.title: Near-term definition of done
docs.text:
Meta-Evolve has a credible first release when a user can define a task, seed artifact, proposer, and evaluator through the canonical small API; choose a search and context policy; run callable and SDK-backed proposers in appropriate execution profiles; evaluate immutable successors; inspect exact causal experience; resume durable runs after failure; and compare runs under equal budgets.

Everything beyond that should extend the same contracts rather than replace the kernel.

docs.title: User-owned live SDK track
docs.text:
Status: Experimental/live-only. Meta-Evolve ships no provider client or credentialed launcher. Use the shipped SDK-integration guide to wrap your own client as a callable or structural proposer.

The current examples are credential-free and deterministic. Their injection points can be used by an opt-in maintainer driver:

Exercise Injection point Maximum wrapper calls Repository proposal examples/agents/user_owned_sdk 1 Experience A/B examples/agents/experience_ab 4 Held-out skill evolution examples/domains/skill_evolution 6

The ceiling is a declaration for a driver, not permission to spend. The driver must identify its wrapper and behavior-affecting configuration, authenticate outside Meta-Evolve, require explicit opt-in, and preserve SDK-specific tools, permissions, timeouts, and telemetry at the edge.

Only shared Meta-Evolve facts are comparable: task, seed, evaluator, effective budget, search declaration, durable usage, failures, lineage, and audited experience. A provider or infrastructure failure, timeout, invalid candidate, missing derivation, or grader failure carries no score and must never be converted to zero.

There is no official provider capture pending. A user may perform one authorized run with their own wrapper. Any published capture must name the wrapper declaration and retain ties, failures, and regressions honestly. CI uses deterministic fixtures and performs no credentialed execution.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This roadmap grows Meta-Evolve through small, testable vertical slices. Every milestone must produce a runnable demonstration, preserve the contracts established by earlier milestones, and add only the infrastructure required by its acceptance tests.

The first product target is a local, extensible improvement system in which a user can define an artifact, task, evaluator, proposer, search policy, and context policy; run a bounded experiment; let agents inspect prior work; replay or resume the run; and compare results under equal budgets. Harness evolution, meta-evolution, trusted concurrency, and federation build on that local product.

The harness-evolution demonstration (milestone 8) is the flagship product demo — "point this at your agent and eval set, get a measurably better agent, and inspect exactly why each change was kept." Earlier milestones should keep that demonstration in view rather than treating it as a distant capstone.

Before the numbered milestones, a disposable API spike validated the user-facing interface against both deterministic code and a real model. The spike is a design probe, not a shortcut into the durable implementation. It is complete; see its status below.

docs.title: Development rules
docs.text:
1. Every milestone has one canonical example that runs with a documented command.
  2. Every new port has an in-memory or deterministic reference adapter and a conformance suite.
  3. The coordinator contains no branches for particular artifact types, proposers, evaluators, or search policies.
  4. Durable behavior is specified through domain events and observable results, not adapter internals.
  5. New infrastructure is introduced only when a milestone's proof requires it.
  6. Failures remain typed: poor task performance, invalid output, timeout, resource exhaustion, policy violation, and infrastructure failure are not interchangeable.
  7. Tests are deterministic by default. Tests requiring credentials, network access, or hardened infrastructure are explicitly separated.
  8. Each milestone updates examples, tests, and user-facing documentation together.
  9. The programming model is the canonical public API contract; other documents link to it rather than redefining signatures.
  10. Canonical examples are first-class user-facing documentation, not test fixtures: each must be short, copy-pasteable, and runnable from a clean checkout, and the simple callable path never requires or surfaces kernel vocabulary such as Trial, OperatorSpec, or WorkItem.

docs.title: Pre-milestone API spike
docs.text: Status: Shipped (July 16, 2026). Both demonstrations ran through the same small public surface under experiments/00_api_spike/, including a real gpt-5.4-mini Codex SDK prompt-optimization run. The exit gate passed: findings are recorded in real_model_findings.md and folded into the current programming model. Closed by #23.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Exercise the smallest declarative API before durable domain models and package boundaries are fixed.

docs.title: Demonstrations
docs.text:
Build a disposable one-to-three-file implementation that runs:

  1. deterministic integer improvement with Greedy and BestOfN;
  2. one real-model prompt-optimization task whose proposer and evaluator each require only a small user function.

The spike should test the canonical Task, meta.run, proposer, evaluator, search, and Run.best()/lineage() surface from the programming model.

docs.title: Questions it must answer
docs.text:
• Can a plain callable be used as a proposer and evaluator in local mode?
  • Is the distinction between task, seed, proposer, evaluator, and search obvious in working code?
  • Does changing search policy require no change to task or proposer code?
  • Can failures and multi-metric evaluations be represented without exposing orchestration machinery?
  • Which values must become durable records, and which abstractions are premature?

docs.title: Exit gate
docs.text:
• Both examples run through the same small public surface.
  • The programming model is revised from observed use rather than aspiration alone.
  • Any deliberately unsupported capability is named explicitly.
  • None of the spike's internal structure becomes a kernel contract without Milestone 1 justification.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Replay, crash recovery, ports and adapters, stable schemas, experience grants, workspace isolation, provider portability, and production-quality model integration.

docs.title: Common definition of done
docs.text:
A milestone is complete only when:

  • its canonical example runs from a clean checkout;
  • its acceptance tests pass locally and in CI where the required capabilities are available;
  • events, artifacts, evaluations, and policy decisions retain causal lineage;
  • public contracts and durable schemas are documented and versioned;
  • newly added adapters pass their conformance suites;
  • resource use and failure outcomes are observable;
  • no later-milestone infrastructure was added speculatively;
  • the next milestone can build on the result without replacing the kernel.

docs.title: Release checkpoints
docs.text:
Checkpoint Included milestones Meaning Kernel proof 1–3 The abstractions compose, policies are replaceable, and agents can reuse prior experience. Durable local engine 4–6 Runs persist, real code can execute, and one SDK agent works end to end. Local v1 7 Several artifact domains use one public kernel without special cases. Evolution system 8–9.5 Harnesses and search policies can be evaluated as artifacts under external controls, then use replayable iterative frontier and tree search. Local author experience 10 Experiments are easier to declare, diagnose, and inspect through stable typed and optional read-only surfaces. Distributed v2 11 Trusted workers execute concurrently with correct leases, retries, and budgets. Federated direction 12 Independent installations exchange authorized, verifiable experience.

The roadmap issue #12 descriptions of M6 closure and the durable-local-engine checkpoint are historical: first-party SDK adapters were superseded before 1.0 by the user-owned callable boundary. The underlying durability and local engine claims remain current.

docs.title: GitHub tracking
docs.text:
The implementation roadmap issue tracks the release checkpoints. Each milestone issue is an acceptance epic and can be decomposed into smaller implementation issues when work begins.

Milestone Issue spike #23 — Pre-milestone API spike (complete) 1 #1 — Deterministic in-memory kernel (complete) 2 #2 — Replaceable search policies (complete) 3 #3 — Shared experience and agent-directed exploration (complete) 4 #4 — Durable local runs and crash recovery (complete) 5 #5 — Executable artifacts and external evaluation (complete) 6 #6 — Native-first SDK proposer portability (complete) 7 #7 — Cross-domain generality and local v1 (complete) 8 #8 — Typed harness evolution 8.7 #150 — Audited prior-candidate source inspection 9 #9 — Policy artifacts and meta-evolution 9.5 #144 — Iterative frontier and tree search policies 10 #149 — Streamline the local author API and inspection experience (complete) 11 #10 — Trusted concurrency and distributed workers 12 #11 — Contributed and federated experience exchange

docs.title: Milestone 1: deterministic kernel
docs.text: Status: Shipped (July 21, 2026; #1, #32). The canonical number search, exact budget accounting, retained-event projection rebuild, built-in Greedy decision reproduction, failure replay, and the remaining acceptance tests now pass. Restart and resume were deliberately deferred to, and are now shipped by, Milestone 4.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Prove the smallest complete improvement loop without language models, subprocesses, databases, or distributed workers.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text:
An integer artifact begins away from a hidden target. Deterministic proposers add or subtract fixed values, a pure evaluator rewards proximity to the target, and a sequential coordinator runs until its evaluation budget is exhausted or the target is reached.

select parent
  → allocate bounded work
  → produce proposal
  → create successor artifact
  → evaluate with evidence
  → append events
  → update projected state
  → choose the next action

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• Frozen, serializable domain models for tasks, artifacts, proposals, trials, trial outcomes, evaluations, evidence, budgets, usage, policies, and typed events; a work-item delivery record stays internal to the kernel and out of user-facing types.
  • Opaque typed identifiers and schema versions on durable envelopes.
  • In-memory artifact and event stores.
  • A deterministic callable proposer adapter and pure-function evaluator adapter.
  • A sequential coordinator that validates transitions, authority, and budgets.
  • A minimal SearchProgram.next(state) decision contract; remaining budget is part of projected state.
  • Typed OperatorSpec values produced by operator policies rather than durable raw strings.
  • Logical ordering, deterministic tie-breaking, and recorded named random substreams.
  • examples/learn/number_search/ with a documented run command.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• The same task, initial artifact, policy, seed, and budget produce the same logical decisions and final projected state.
  • Every artifact and evaluation can be traced to the trial, proposal, and search decision that caused it.
  • Trial identity remains distinct from duplicate delivery or completion attempts.
  • Duplicate completion is idempotent.
  • Exhausted budgets prevent additional work.
  • Invalid proposals and evaluator failures are recorded without being treated as low scores.
  • The run can be rebuilt from its event stream without agent-local state.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Reachable and unreachable target scenarios.
  • Exact evaluation and usage accounting.
  • Deterministic replay from an empty projection.
  • Decision reproduction with the same named random substreams and trial seeds.
  • Optimistic append conflict in the in-memory event store.
  • Duplicate work completion.
  • Invalid transition and budget-exhaustion rejection.
  • Failure taxonomy serialization and replay.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: SQLite, filesystem persistence, subprocesses, real agents, semantic search, snapshots, concurrency, and user interfaces beyond the example command.

docs.title: Milestone 2: replaceable search policies
docs.text: Status: Shipped. M1 supplies the Greedy baseline and the generic preparation boundary. M2.1 adds durable archive decisions, linked decision explanations, and the first reusable policy-contract gate. M2.2 adds the public BestOfN(max_trials=20) preset, independent seed expansion, and historical decision reproduction through the same contract. M2.3 adds the public Population(size=3, tournament_size=2, max_trials=20) preset with explicit rank-ordered archive membership, deterministic tournament selection, and a corridor test showing retention of a temporarily worse branch. M2.4 adds strict compatible-run comparison and the canonical equal-budget three-policy benchmark.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Prove that search behavior is a replaceable policy and that different policies can be compared fairly without changing the coordinator.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text: Run independent best-of-N, greedy hill climbing, and a small population policy against the same integer task, initial artifact, seed rules, and evaluation budget. Produce a comparison report containing best score, evaluations, usage, and lineage references.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• Independent best-of-N policy.
  • The M1 Greedy baseline covered by the shared M2 policy conformance suite.
  • Small population retention policy.
  • Deterministic selection and tie-breaking rules.
  • Explicit admission, stopping, and budget-allocation decisions.
  • A run-comparison projection or report.
  • One publishable benchmark example: an honest, reproducible equal-budget comparison (for example, greedy with context reuse versus independent best-of-N) presented as a notebook or report a reader can rerun, serving as the project's first credibility artifact.
  • examples/learn/policy_comparison/.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• Policies consume the same projected state and return typed decisions.
  • Replacing a policy requires no coordinator, runtime, evaluator, or storage changes.
  • Every policy decision records its inputs, policy version, rationale metadata, and observed logical step.
  • Comparisons normalize results by the same declared budget.
  • A policy cannot directly mutate projections or grant itself additional budget.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• All three policies pass one shared policy conformance suite.
  • Equal inputs produce deterministic decisions.
  • Tie cases have stable outcomes.
  • Population admission and eviction replay correctly.
  • A historical policy decision can be reproduced without future evaluations.
  • Adding a minimal test policy requires only implementing the policy contract.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Pareto archives, novelty search, islands, bandits, MCTS, learned allocation, and policy evolution.

docs.title: M2.4 completion
docs.text:
Run.summary() and Run.compare() are immutable derived views over committed records. Fair comparison requires identical evaluator/proposer declarations, primary objective, task and effective run budgets, artifact kind, and initial artifact declaration and digest. Policy choice, policy configuration, and root seed may differ; exact primary scores tie without a usage or policy tiebreaker.

The canonical examples/learn/policy_comparison/ sweep uses target 12, moves (-2, 1, 5), initial value 0, nine evaluations, eight successor trials, and root seeds 0 through 39. Its executed notebook reports complete score and usage distributions and representative star, chain, and tree-branch lineages, with an explicit small-illustration evidence disclaimer. The companion executed milestone_2_tour.ipynb introduces M2.1 through M2.4 from the public callable path before showing optional kernel-level inspection.

docs.title: Milestone 3: shared experience and agent-directed exploration
docs.text: Status: Shipped (July 24, 2026; #3). M3.1 adds the read-only temporal experience projection, M3.2 adds bounded replayable policy-pushed context, M3.3 adds audited, strictly-prior agent-pulled access, and M3.4 adds declared derivation, run-aggregate experience usage, memory-strategy comparison, and the canonical four-variant demonstration.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Make prior trials useful to later agents through both policy-pushed context and agent-pulled investigation.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text: Agent A produces several failed trials. Agent B searches those trials, opens a relevant proposal and evaluation, compares siblings, and uses the observed failure to choose a successful transformation. The new proposal records the exact experience B observed and used.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• An in-memory ExperienceGraph projection with occurrence-based node, ancestor, child, inclusive-sibling, causal-leaf frontier, trace, and inclusive historical state_at queries.
  • A scoped, read-only ExperienceReader with exact filtering and traversal.
  • ExperienceGrant bounds for task, run, logical time, result count, context size, and resource use; identity and visibility remain single-user stubs.
  • ContextPolicy implementations for NoMemory, AncestorsOnly, and BestSibling.
  • Events for automatic context selection, experience queries, opened records, and comparisons.
  • Immutable ContextBundle records and exact query-result records, including ordering and truncation.
  • Stable references from observed experience into Proposal.derived_from.
  • examples/learn/experience_reuse/ covering push-only, pull-only, and combined access.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• Agents distinguish experience that existed from experience they actually observed.
  • An as_of argument may narrow but never widen a work item's logical-time grant.
  • Cross-task, out-of-run, retracted, or future experience is not returned.
  • M3.2 context selection obeys record and rendering bounds without consuming task usage; M3.3 pull operations count against their ExperienceGrant.
  • The derivation graph remains acyclic while semantic relationships may be typed cross-links.
  • Content deduplication does not collapse distinct causal occurrences.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Agent B improves by consulting Agent A's recorded failure.
  • Push-only, pull-only, combined, and no-memory variants run under equal budgets.
  • Ancestor, sibling, and historical-state queries return expected results.
  • Attempts to cross task, run, or logical-time boundaries fail.
  • Query result limits and usage limits are enforced.
  • Replay reconstructs the same observed-context references and derived-from edges.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Embeddings, vector databases, learned retrieval, graph databases, filesystem projections, principal-based authorization, licensing enforcement, and cross-installation experience.

docs.title: M3.1 completion
docs.text:
replay_experience_graph() derives one trial-centered node per committed trial occurrence through the validated run replay path. ExperienceRef uses the run, record kind, and existing occurrence identity; identical artifact payloads therefore remain distinct causal occurrences. Exact decision, explanation, proposal, artifact-creation, outcome, evidence, evaluation, and completed-trial records are retained without defining another lifecycle.

Queries are scoped by task, run, and an optional inclusive logical step. Ancestors exclude self, siblings include self, frontier means visible causal leaves rather than archive membership, and a trace spans the target trial and its accessible ancestors while preserving committed event order with a fixed intra-event kind order. Missing, wrong-kind, cross-scope, future, hidden, retracted, and synthetic non-local direct targets all receive one opaque denial. Collection reads omit inaccessible occurrences and do not traverse through them.

Only ExperienceRef is durable and exported through meta_evolve.domain. Graph and query views remain outside the package-root callable API. M3.1 adds no reader grant, pushed context, retrieval, durable graph store, authentication, licensing, or proposal-derivation contract.

docs.title: M3.2 completion
docs.text:
meta.run(context=...) accepts NoMemory, AncestorsOnly, BestSibling, or a compatible declared policy. None and NoMemory() preserve pre-M3.2 identity, stream, trial specs, and proposer behavior except that the internal ProposerContext now exposes a synthesized empty bundle. Non-default configuration contributes one final serialized ContextSpec identity segment.

ContextPolicyDeclared follows bootstrap evaluation. A transparent search-program wrapper stamps its policy reference only into successor specs, and a generic coordinator operation commits one ContextSelected after the decision explanation and before proposer invocation. Bundles snapshot exact typed records, stable reference order, canonical rendering, reason, truncation, and ContextUsage; record and character bounds are independent from task Usage.

AncestorsOnly flattens accessible ancestors in graph-node and committed-record order. BestSibling excludes the current node, ranks only successful sibling evaluations through rank_evaluations, and preserves completion-order ties. Replay validates the committed records against their strictly prior visible sources and returns the committed bundle without rerunning selection or rendering. Context declaration and selection facts remain inspectable in the experience graph but cannot themselves become policy candidates.

docs.title: M3.3 completion
docs.text:
meta.run(experience=...) accepts the run-level ExperienceAccess protocol; PullAccess(max_operations=20, max_results=20, max_records=100, max_chars=32_000) is the shipped declaration. None normalizes completely away. A non-default access declaration contributes the final serialized ExperienceSpec identity segment after any ContextSpec.

Every successor receives a fresh immutable ExperienceGrant bounded to the same task/run and as_of=trial.logical_step - 1. Its ExperienceReader supports exact conjunctive search filters, open, ancestors, inclusive siblings, and right-minus-left numeric comparison. Results preserve committed ordering, exact structured snapshots, canonical prefix-bounded rendering, truncation, and cumulative operation/result/record/character usage. Failed evaluations remain inspectable and never become synthetic losses.

The audited lifecycle is grant → (attempt → success|denial|exhaustion)* → proposal. Attempts charge before validation, opaque denials disclose no protected content, and over-ceiling calls receive a separate content-free exception. Replay validates authority, placement, reproducible operation identities, cumulative charging, and terminal matching, and holds every success to the shared deterministic contract: records must equal committed sources inside the effective boundary, references must stay visible, deltas must derive from the paired records, and rendering must prefix the canonical rendering of the committed records. Selection, traversal, filtering, and comparison logic is never re-run, and committed outcomes are returned directly. Context and pull-audit facts remain graph-inspectable but are excluded from both push and pull candidate sets, and naming them in a search filter is a malformed request. Pull usage does not change task budgets, logical steps, or named randomness.

docs.title: M3.4 completion
docs.text:
Proposal and callable ProposalResult now carry an explicit ordered derived_from declaration. One shared pure validator reconstructs pushed and pulled observations from committed records and requires a unique, strictly-prior same-run subsequence. Resource exhaustion precedes derivation policy failure; both coordinator-imposed failures clear edges and commit no candidate. Valid typed proposer failures and failed independent evaluations retain their declared lineage.

Canonical serialization omits empty derivation and rejects an explicitly encoded empty default, so old proposal, event, context, and replay bytes remain unchanged at schema version 1. RunExperienceUsage, Run.experience_usage(), and expanded summaries report context and pull totals. Comparisons continue to require equal task/run budgets and core declarations while allowing different memory strategies, with exact declaration-match flags.

The runnable examples/learn/experience_reuse/ experiment gives no-memory, push-only, pull-only, and combined variants the same task, proposer, evaluator, chain search, seed, and task/run budget. It records early evaluator failures, then succeeds only when prior failure evidence is reused and cited. Replay reconstructs the same derivation edges. The companion executed milestone_3_tour.ipynb introduces M3.1 through M3.4 from the public callable path, with push_pull_lab.ipynb and derivation_comparison_lab.ipynb as focused kernel-level labs.

docs.title: Milestone 4: durable local runs and crash recovery
docs.text: Status: Shipped (July 24, 2026; #4, #47). Durable artifacts and events, atomic commit, verified manifests, corruption detection, migration, recovery-frontier replay, and context/experience-aware resume satisfy the acceptance gate without changing the M1–M3 logical identities or trajectories.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Persist the kernel without changing its logical behavior and prove that interrupted runs resume safely.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text: Start a deterministic run, complete several trials, terminate the process, rebuild the coordinator and projections from disk, resume from the committed frontier, and compare the outcome with an uninterrupted run.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• SQLite append-only event store with optimistic concurrency.
  • Content-addressed filesystem artifact store.
  • Durable run, trial, population, work-item, usage, and experience projections.
  • Stable idempotency keys and committed logical steps.
  • A resume command or documented API.
  • Migration/versioning strategy for durable schemas.
  • examples/operations/crash_recovery/.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• SQLite and in-memory adapters satisfy the same event-store contract.
  • Identical payload bytes reuse content identity while occurrence provenance remains distinct.
  • Only atomically committed object records and transition events affect reconstructed state.
  • Restarting does not repeat completed logical work or lose remaining budget.
  • Historical state is initially reconstructed from immutable object records and transition events; snapshots are optional future caches.
  • Corrupt or incompatible durable data fails explicitly rather than being silently ignored.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Interrupted and uninterrupted deterministic runs reach equivalent logical results.
  • Restart before and after each important transition.
  • Duplicate completion across a restart.
  • Optimistic concurrency conflicts across two store clients.
  • Artifact deduplication with distinct causal occurrences.
  • Projection rebuild from empty projection tables using durable object records and transition events.
  • Durable schema-version rejection and supported migration tests.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Graph databases, remote databases, object stores, parallel workers, filesystem snapshots, and backup services.

docs.title: Milestone 5: executable artifacts and external evaluation
docs.text: Status: Shipped (July 24, 2026). M5.4 closes the canonical script, executed notebook, integrated acceptance, durable-query, and documentation gates without adding a production API or widening the development sandbox.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Safely enough for development, execute candidate source artifacts in private workspaces while keeping evaluation outside candidate authority.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text: A deterministic patch agent improves a small Python function. Each candidate is materialized into its own workspace and evaluated by external unit tests that the candidate cannot modify.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• [x] Immutable SourceTree with stable utf8-tree-v1 digesting.
  • [x] Synchronous directory-copy WorkspaceProvider for materialize, capture, and dispose.
  • [x] Exact-file TextPatch, rich PatchResult, and workspace-backed PatchProposer.
  • [x] Generic ProposerRunner seam preserving the decoded callable path.
  • [x] Clearly named development subprocess SandboxProvider with timeouts and captured output.
  • [x] External evaluator adapter with versioned environment and evidence.
  • [x] Typed process outcomes for success, timeout, resource exhaustion, policy violation, infrastructure failure, and task failure.
  • [x] examples/domains/python_function/.
  • [x] Executed milestone_5_tour.ipynb with deterministic semantic output.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• Every work item receives a private writable workspace derived from an immutable parent.
  • Capturing changes produces a new immutable artifact without altering its parent.
  • Evaluator code and hidden tests remain outside the candidate mutation boundary.
  • Process execution and task evaluation failures remain distinguishable.
  • Workspace cleanup runs after success and failure.
  • Durable local history remains queryable, while cold resume of local workspace components fails explicitly with CapabilityError.
  • The subprocess adapter makes no claim to safely execute untrusted community code.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Passing, failing, invalid, and unchanged patches.
  • Parent immutability after workspace capture.
  • Timeout and process-output capture.
  • Workspace cleanup after evaluator or runtime failure.
  • Candidate attempts to modify external evaluator inputs.
  • Stable source-tree digests and artifact round trips.
  • Workspace and sandbox adapter conformance suites.

The acceptance suite pins the broken and repaired content digests, scores 0 → 1, process exits 1 → 0, evidence kinds, winning lineage, reopened best/lineage equivalence, clean-checkout script output, and temporary notebook re-execution. It also proves a failed cold resume leaves events, artifacts, and both workspace trees unchanged. The exact development boundary is unchanged: patch traversal is rejected, capture excludes the grader, and the canonical run leaves grader bytes intact; hostile-runtime filesystem isolation is not claimed.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Containers, hardened untrusted execution, Git worktree optimization, remote volumes, real LLM agents, multi-repository artifacts, and portable runtime reconstruction.

docs.title: Milestone 6: SDK proposer boundary proof
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. M6 completed on July 28, 2026. It proved that native coding SDKs could produce ordinary candidates through the existing proposer seam without adding provider vocabulary or branches to the coordinator.

The first-party Claude and Codex adapters, package extras, and provider-specific capture fixtures were superseded before 1.0 by the smaller user-owned SDK boundary and have now been removed. Their detailed implementation and live measurements remain available in Git history and closed issues #57–#93, but they are not part of the current source tree or acceptance surface.

docs.title: Shipped outcome
docs.text:
• Plain callables and structural propose(parent, context) objects share one runner, preflight, accounting, evidence, and failure path.
  • ProposerContext exposes exact candidate-visible context and optional audited experience without task authority.
  • User code owns SDK authentication, sessions, tools, permissions, retries, output decoding, and provider telemetry.
  • Meta-Evolve owns candidate validation, independent evaluation, budgets, durable lineage, experience auditing, and promotion authority.
  • No provider dependency, extra, compatibility shim, generic provider runtime, or provider-specific coordinator behavior ships.

docs.title: Acceptance boundary
docs.text: Current deterministic tests prove the structural callable seam, configured component identity, typed SDK-wrapper failures, usage validation, pushed context, audited pull delegation, and declared derivation. Provider behavior is validated only by an explicitly authorized milestone-owned experiment when a current acceptance gate requires it.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: A first-party provider adapter, cross-provider option model, generic agent runtime, durable provider session, automatic retry, portable live component reconstruction, or provider parity claim.

docs.title: Milestone 7: generality proof and local v1
docs.text:
Historical annotation. M7's provider-conformance references describe the then-shipped M6 adapters. They were superseded by the user-owned callable boundary on August 5, 2026; M7's artifact-domain and local-kernel acceptance evidence remains current.

Status: Shipped (August 2, 2026; #7, PRs #94–#97). Four artifact domains — number, text, repository, and skill set — reach the coordinator through one meta.run call site and leave an identical kernel record, with four distinct kinds over three representations (tests/test_four_domain_kernel.py). No domain needed a coordinator branch, and the proving phase changed no file under src/. A static gate holds the property open: application modules import no concrete adapter outside a justified wiring allowlist, and nothing dispatches on a concrete artifact type outside the codecs and the adapters (tests/test_application_purity.py). The add-a-domain walkthrough is docs/adding-an-artifact-domain.md; its code blocks are one script, executed in a fresh interpreter from an empty directory and compared against the output the page claims, so the documentation walkthrough cannot drift from the library.

Three deliverables landed differently from their wording above, and the difference is not absorbed into it:

  • Extension contracts. M7 added the ArtifactCodec contract and the optional RunIndex capability, and changed ProposalResult to carry an artifact value rather than a frozen payload. The runtime, evaluator, workspace, and sandbox ports and the search- and context-policy contracts already existed and gained no members here.
  • Commands. The command line ships five verbs, not four: list joins run, inspect, resume, and compare. Run ids are content-derived digests rather than names anyone retypes from memory, so without enumeration every other verb becomes unreachable once an id leaves the terminal. It rests on one new read-only storage surface, Storage.runs().
  • Conformance utilities covered two of the seven component types. At the M7 gate meta_evolve.conformance published suites for artifact codecs and for repository-editing proposers only. Search policies, workspaces, and sandboxes kept reusable function-based suites under tests/ that were not published; evaluators and context policies had concrete tests and no reusable suite at all. An extension author writing any of those five had nothing to subclass.

Historical annotation. That gap is closed. The follow-up in #98 converted the workspace and sandbox contracts, retired policy_contract.py by widening M9's SearchProgramTests with a search_factory fixture, and added EvaluatorTests and ContextPolicyTests, so all seven families now have published subclassable suites alongside the typed MutationSurfaceTests. The same closure root-exported the read-only ExperienceGraph plus its query, node, record, and state values so a third-party context policy can implement the typed protocol without importing replay internals. The function modules tests/policy_contract.py, tests/workspace_contract.py, and tests/sandbox_contract.py were removed in the same change rather than left to drift beside their published replacements. This annotation does not widen the M7 gate, which was accepted on the two-family state described above.

docs.title: The defect-repair pass (July 30 – August 2, 2026)
docs.text:
Building the shipped domain and agent examples and hardening their reopening path exposed six defects in M7's own deliverables. Each is backed by something that actually broke while measuring, not by review speculation, and three turned real measurements into misleading ones. They are recorded here rather than deferred because a milestone that ships a misleading measurement has not met its own acceptance gate.

defect what it cost closed by No public accessor for a losing attempt six examples reached into run._projection() or inferred failure from evaluation_count; two invented "no candidate" as a reason for what was really a timeout Run.trials() and TrialView.state A missing extra became a per-candidate score a CapabilityError in an evaluator surfaced as NoSuccessfulEvaluation, blaming the candidate for the machine CapabilityError reserved as abort control flow at both boundaries A hardcoded turn limit measured itself three corrupted measurements, including an A/B that lost 7 of 8 control reps Claude(max_turns=…, pull_max_turns=…) compare could not see a model inside an evaluator closure a winner reported for an uncontrolled comparison name_only_components reports it; ComponentRef.configured_local lets a caller close it The comparison refusal was untyped a bare ValueError escaped the command line's translation and reached the user as a traceback RunsNotComparable, a RunError carrying the declaration that differed A stored custom-domain local run could not be decoded after restart durable storage outlived the live codec index, but Run(id, storage) knew built-ins only keyword-only Run(..., registry=...) reconstructs the read-only codec index without granting execution authority

Reopening a closed milestone sets a precedent, so the justification is narrow and stated rather than assumed. These are repairs to M7's own shipped surface, found by M7's own acceptance examples, and they add no milestone scope. The passage below about Pi integration and filesystem-shaped experience is not a general convention authorizing this — it is specific to those two post-M6 follow-ups. Anything that is genuinely new capability belongs in M8.

Two things this pass deliberately did not do. It did not raise either turn limit: the defaults emit byte-identical native profiles, so a run recorded before the pass still replays. That statement is about the library's defaults only. Any run that declares a turn ceiling declares a different component, and its component.version and RunId move accordingly — which is correct, and is why compare refuses two runs whose ceilings differ. The experience_ab, adversarial_inputs, prompt_optimization, and model_migration examples all declare one, so all four moved; model_migration's evaluator identity moved for a second, independent reason. And it did not make compare infer a configuration it was never told about — compare still refuses only on what a run declared, which is why the gap is reported as well as made closeable.

One tightening in the same pass is not a defect repair, so it is recorded apart from the table. Registry.register_artifact_type now refuses a kind, representation, or declared interface name that is empty or carries outer whitespace, through the same _require_text the rest of the domain uses. An empty interfaces tuple stays valid and means the codec declares no consumer-facing interface. These fields reach durable records and content-derived ids, so registration refuses a bad declaration rather than normalizing it — a silently trimmed kind would encode artifacts under a name its own author never wrote. The observable change for an extension author is the exception type: a non-string kind raised TypeError before this pass and raises ValueError now, so declaration validity is one error family instead of two.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Demonstrate that the kernel is a reusable framework rather than an implementation specialized for one artifact or task domain.

docs.title: Canonical demonstrations
docs.text:
Run four use cases through the same coordinator:

  1. deterministic number search;
  2. text or prompt optimization;
  3. repository/code improvement;
  4. skill-set evolution.

Only artifact codecs, task definitions, proposers, evaluators, and policy configuration may differ between the examples.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• Public extension contracts for artifact codecs, runtimes, evaluators, search policies, context policies, workspaces, and sandboxes.
  • A small artifact-type registry with schema validation and declared interfaces.
  • Text/prompt and skill-set artifact implementations.
  • Minimal user-facing API and commands to run, inspect, resume, and compare experiments.
  • Adapter conformance-test utilities for extension authors.
  • A concise tutorial for adding a new artifact domain.
  • examples/domains/text_optimization/ and examples/domains/skill_evolution/.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• No coordinator branch checks a concrete artifact type, provider, evaluator, or policy.
  • A new domain is added by registering implementations behind existing contracts.
  • All examples expose comparable lineage, budgets, evaluations, and experience views.
  • Users can inspect why a candidate exists, what an agent observed, and why it was evaluated or admitted.
  • A clean local installation can run deterministic examples without provider credentials.
  • Provider-dependent examples fail with actionable setup guidance.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Run all four domains through one shared kernel test harness.
  • Static or behavioral check that the coordinator imports no concrete adapters or artifact implementations.
  • Create a minimal custom artifact/evaluator in a test without modifying core packages.
  • Public API serialization and schema-version tests.
  • CLI smoke tests for run, inspect, resume, and compare.
  • Documentation walkthrough from a clean environment.

docs.title: Exit gate
docs.text: If a use case requires a domain-specific coordinator branch, stop and repair the abstraction before beginning harness evolution. Passing this gate defines the local v1 architecture.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
Complete harness mutation, policy evolution, concurrency, remote workers, federation, dashboards, and plugin marketplaces.

Pi integration and filesystem-shaped experience are post-M6 follow-ups. They do not retroactively widen M6's portability or conformance gate and enter M7 only through separately accepted issues.

docs.title: Milestone 8: harness evolution
docs.text: Status: Shipped (closed August 14, 2026; #8). The deterministic implementation through M8.5 and #124 shipped on harness-manifest-v1. M8.6's authorized SDK captures — the first rejected by strict schema validation before native mutation decoding, and later runs that reached the v1 successor-validation boundary — are retained only in the closed, unmerged PR #162; no additional harness code beyond M8.5 merged to main. #8 closed on that retained historical evidence, without claiming any live validation beyond what M8.5 shipped. The canonical example is examples/research/harness_evolution/.

docs.title: Executable subissue program
docs.text:
• [x] M8.0: lock development-only search, seed-only held-out evaluation, the core-side successor hook, immutable surface declarations, evaluator identity, outer-boundary resume, and the one-fixture evidence limit.
  • [x] M8.1: ship agent-harness / harness-manifest-v1, both mutation surfaces, their published conformance suite, and the core bypass rejection.
  • [x] M8.2: ship portable repository episodes, explicit splits, stable digests, hidden evaluator tests, captured attempts, and nested accounting.
  • [x] M8.3: implement user-owned structured-output TFD as an ordinary callable; no core optimizer, provider adapter, or agent runtime was added.
  • [x] M8.4: add strict seed-only held-out comparison and external eligibility reporting.
  • [x] #124: add staged, digest-preserving, symlink-refusing harness export.
  • [x] M8.5: run the deterministic durable flagship with development quality 0.0 → 0.5 → 1.0, held-out 0.0 → 1.0, and committed-episode recovery.
  • [x] M8.6: retain the first authorized schema-failure capture without improving its outcome, plus later authorized runs that reached native mutation decoding and successor validation. Both records exist only in the closed, unmerged PR #162.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Treat an executable agent harness as a typed composite artifact whose permitted components can be improved under external evaluation and promotion controls.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text:
A worker harness performs held-out tasks. An outer agent investigates earlier harness source and traces, then modifies one or two declared surfaces—initially a planner prompt and context policy. External evaluation determines whether the successor is admitted.

The outer agent is injected as a user-owned callable. CI uses a deterministic fixture-backed SDK client; an opt-in maintainer driver may call a real SDK through the same boundary. The first authorized live run is captured once, sanitized, and retained with ties, regressions, and failures intact. Evaluation, equal budgets, mutation authority, and promotion stay outside the wrapper. See the boundary decision.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• HarnessArtifact manifest containing component references and declared interfaces.
  • Typed parameters for initial mutable surfaces such as TextParam and PolicyParam.
  • Explicit MutationSurface separating candidate-controlled components from hidden evaluation, secrets, permissions, budgets, audit history, and promotion policy.
  • Harness materialization, execution, capture, and validation.
  • Held-out task split and promotion rule.
  • Harness-specific comparison views over quality, cost, and failure behavior.
  • examples/research/harness_evolution/.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• A candidate can modify only manifest-declared mutable surfaces.
  • Component references and the composite harness both retain content identity and causal lineage.
  • Harness evaluation runs fresh executions rather than trusting self-reported improvements.
  • Failed or invalid harnesses remain inspectable experience.
  • Later agents can compare complete harness code and traces, not only summary feedback.
  • Additional mutation surfaces can be registered without changing the coordinator.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Valid prompt and context-policy mutations.
  • Rejection of hidden-evaluator, permission, budget, and promotion-policy changes.
  • Composite artifact digest and provenance tests.
  • Fresh held-out evaluation and deterministic fixture tests.
  • Comparison against the unchanged baseline harness under equal budgets.
  • Resume and replay of a harness-evolution run.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: All mutation surfaces at once, unrestricted self-modification, automatic promotion to production, policy meta-evolution, and claims of general recursive self-improvement.

docs.title: Milestone 8.7: audited prior-candidate source inspection
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). Tracked by #150. This is an independent post-M8 follow-up, not an M8 closure gate, and it does not change M8.6 or M9.5.

The ordered program is M8.7.1 → M8.7.2 → M8.7.3 → M8.7.4 → M8.7.5:

  • [x] #155 — M8.7.1: proved the value of exact prior source using existing durable evidence in examples/agents/prior_source_inspection/.
  • [x] #158 — M8.7.2: shipped August 18, 2026. It locks the public, accounting, replay, and Git-neutral manifest contracts.
  • [x] #159 — M8.7.3: shipped August 18, 2026. It adds bounded audited source path listing and reads while source diff and history projection remain unavailable.
  • [x] #160 — M8.7.4: shipped August 18, 2026. It adds a canonical library-owned source diff.
  • [x] #161 — M8.7.5: shipped August 18, 2026. It projects authorized manifests into a disposable read-only Git history view.

Source access remains same-task, same-run, strictly prior, occurrence-based, bounded by the existing experience grant, and reconstructed from committed observations. Git is a presentation adapter, never durable identity or part of the candidate artifact. Cross-run libraries, semantic retrieval, whole-tree reads, and coordinator branches remain out of scope.

docs.title: M8.7.2 contract boundary
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). This stage published advanced durable vocabulary and protocol shape, not a callable source capability. M8.7.3 now implements listing and reading under that contract; M8.7.5 now completes the shipped program.

Historical annotation. M8.7.5 narrowly supersedes this stage's earlier “no new durable event” reservation: truthful replay of a pre-execution mount requires one SourceHistoryMounted fact. The locked reader APIs, accounting, identity and authority rules remain unchanged, including the no Git-mount usage category claim. This is a final-stage repair to M8.7's own locked projection contract, not general permission to reopen shipped milestones.

The scoped ExperienceReader declares these operations; listing and reading ship in M8.7.3 and canonical diffing ships in M8.7.4:

list_source_paths(artifact_ref, *, as_of=None, limit=None) -> SourcePathListing
read_source(artifact_ref, *, paths, as_of=None) -> SourceRead
diff_source(
    older_artifact_ref,
    newer_artifact_ref,
    *,
    paths=(),
    as_of=None,
) -> SourceDiff

Every target is an exact ExperienceRef(kind="artifact") occurrence. Shipped listing, reads, and diffs accept only SourceTree / utf8-tree-v1. ExperienceRequest admits the three operation names and an ordered paths tuple whose empty default is omitted canonically, preserving legacy schema-v3 bytes. Anything other than a tuple of strings is a Python shape error before auditing. Empty reads, duplicates, non-normalized paths, wrong reference kinds, invalid logical time, and inaccessible, missing, future, hidden, retracted, or cross-run content enter the normal audit lifecycle and produce the same opaque denial. One missing requested path atomically denies the complete read.

Authorization and artifact existence precede capacity resolution. Listing and reading reserve one result; diff reserves two. Missing complete result capacity uses the existing opaque exhaustion outcome. Record and character ceilings retain the largest deterministic prefix of complete paths, files, or diff entries—never partial source. Each retained entry charges one record and the character delta is exactly len(rendered). Listings render normalized lexicographic prefixes as compact JSON-string lines. Reads preserve requested order and render compact JSON Lines objects containing exactly path and source, with stable keys, Unicode preserved, and no trailing newline. Diff entries have added, deleted, or modified status and use meta-evolve-unified-diff/v1; M8.7.4 owns that shipped renderer.

SourcePathListing, SourceFile, SourceRead, SourceDiffEntry, and SourceDiff live only in meta_evolve.domain. Every result identifies its authorized occurrence and verified digest, retains complete entries, and carries canonical rendering, truncation state, and cumulative ExperienceUsage. The new standalone records use the current schema-v3 envelope; no migration or global schema bump occurs.

Existing PullAccess defaults remain unchanged. A source-sized profile is only an ordinary outer grant:

from meta_evolve.policies import PullAccess

SOURCE_ACCESS = PullAccess(
    max_operations=40,
    max_results=40,
    max_records=400,
    max_chars=256_000,
)

Human-facing accounting uses canonically ordered, non-zero ExperienceOperationUsage entries in this order: search, open, ancestors, siblings, compare, list_source_paths, read_source, then diff_source. Their dimension-wise sum equals RunExperienceUsage.pull. Manifest construction reuses audited operations, so there is no Git-mount category and no duplicate byte charge. M8.7.3 implements this derived view.

docs.title: M8.7.3 audited source listing and reads
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). AuditedExperienceReader now executes list_source_paths and read_source for exact, visible source-tree / utf8-tree-v1 artifact occurrences. At that stage diff_source remained fail-closed; M8.7.4 now ships it. Git projection, whole-tree reads, semantic retrieval, and cross-run access remain unshipped.

Resolution first proves the occurrence is visible in the same task and run at the effective strictly-prior boundary, then asks the artifact-store edge to revalidate its digest and decode its source tree. Missing, inaccessible, wrong-kind, and unsupported occurrences share one opaque denial. Durable corruption and infrastructure failures remain typed. Reads prove every path exists before reserving result capacity, so one missing path discloses and charges no source content.

One successful listing or read consumes one result. The largest prefix of complete entries fitting caller, record, and character bounds is retained; newlines between entries count, and no path or file is split. A zero-capacity prefix is a truncated success after its result charge. Operation- and result-ceiling exhaustion are durable, cumulative audit outcomes. Replay returns committed outcomes without live resolution, while durable loading independently reproduces every source result from its stored artifact.

Successful listing/read occurrences enter the existing observation ledger and may be cited in Proposal.derived_from; denied, exhausted, or missing-path attempts do not. RunExperienceUsage.by_operation exposes canonical non-zero application views whose dimension-wise sum equals RunExperienceUsage.pull.

Three Git-neutral durable values fix the future history presentation:

SourceHistoryBounds(max_ancestors, max_archive_members, max_chars)
SourceHistoryEntry(
    artifact_ref,
    digest,
    parent_refs,
    logical_step,
    proposal_ref,
    evaluation_ref,
    selection_rationale,
)
SourceHistoryManifest(format_version, head_ref, entries, bounds)

The format is source-history-manifest/v1; head_ref identifies the first entry. Artifact occurrence refs are unique even when their content digests match. All refs have declared kinds and one run, and parent refs remain inside the authorized manifest. Every entry retains the proposal, evaluation, logical step, digest, and rationale explaining its presence. Source bytes, Git IDs or refs, commit metadata, environment values, and repository layout are excluded.

M8.7.5 may present that same authorized history through this future adapter declaration:

meta.PatchProposer(
    edit,
    history=meta_evolve.adapters.GitHistoryView(
        max_ancestors=...,
        max_archive_members=...,
        max_chars=...,
    ),
)

All history bounds are explicit. Experiment(experience=PullAccess(...)) remains the outer authority. At this stage the declaration added no implementation, root export, ninth Experiment field, run() overlay, artifact identity, Git authority, coordinator branch, or parallel proposer runtime.

docs.title: M8.7.4 canonical audited source diffs
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). AuditedExperienceReader.diff_source authorizes and verifies its older then newer exact occurrences through the M8.7.3 source edge before atomically reserving two results. Both operands must be visible, same-task/run, strictly prior source-tree / utf8-tree-v1 occurrences. Successful diffs retain both occurrence refs and verified digests; the observation ledger admits those refs in operand order.
