The pure meta-evolve-unified-diff/v1 renderer compares the sorted changed-path union, with an optional filter that cannot alter output order. It normalizes CRLF and CR to LF while retaining final-terminator state, uses a deterministic Myers line diff with deletion-before-insertion ties, emits three context lines, and merges changes separated by at most six unchanged lines. JSON-encoded file operands, uniform hunk ranges, missing-final-newline markers, complete per-path headers and hunks, and no trailing newline make rendering independent of Git, subprocesses, and platforms.

Record and character ceilings retain the largest ordered prefix of complete entries after the two-result reservation; a first oversized entry is a successful truncated zero-record result, while an empty canonical diff is not truncated. Replay returns committed outcomes without resolving artifacts. Folding validates operand visibility, result shape, canonical ordering, rendering, and exact usage; durable loading independently resolves both stored artifacts and reconstructs the complete expected result. Schema version 3, root exports, Experiment, coordinator dispatch, and proposer constructors are unchanged. At this stage Git history projection remained reserved for M8.7.5.

docs.title: M8.7.5 authorized read-only Git history
docs.text:
Status: Shipped (August 18, 2026). meta_evolve.adapters.GitHistoryView adds an optional PatchProposer(history=...) capability with required ancestor, archive-member, and character bounds. It uses the declared pull grant to audit a complete selected-parent listing, canonical metadata search, ancestor traversal, and complete additional-tree reads. Selection is parent first, then breadth-first causal ancestors, then archive order; duplicate occurrences are removed by first occurrence while equal digests remain distinct.

The resulting source-history-manifest/v1 is committed once as SourceHistoryMounted before callback execution. The fact has no usage delta, operation category, or derivation authority. Replay drives the identical audited prefix from committed outcomes, and durable loading revalidates both the source observations and the reconstructed manifest without retaining Git objects.

Git objects, refs, configuration, index, attributes, hooks, and home live in a disposable external sidecar. The callback receives a meta_evolve.ports.WorkspaceSession with the materialized root, a complete controlled subprocess environment, and the committed manifest. HEAD is the selected parent, causal parents are ordinary commits, and retained archive members have deterministic ephemeral refs. The frozen sidecar is disposed before capture; any direct callback mutation of the source workspace is a PolicyViolation.

GitHistoryView is adapter-only, and changing its version or bounds changes the configured proposer identity. There is no root export, run() overlay, Experiment field, coordinator branch, whole-tree reader operation, cross-run access, semantic retrieval, persistent Git identity, or independent agent runtime.

docs.title: Milestone 9: policy artifacts and meta-evolution
docs.text: Status: Shipped (August 6, 2026). The canonical deterministic example is examples/research/policy_evolution/. M9 depends on the contracts shipped in M8.1–M8.5; it does not depend on #124 or the still-open M8.6 live proof.

docs.title: Executable subissue program
docs.text:
• [x] M9.0: lock dependency, authority, reuse, aggregation, and namespace decisions before implementation.
  • [x] M9.1: ship search-policy / policy-manifest-v1, two fixed mutation surfaces, neutral mutation contracts, and four-surface conformance.
  • [x] M9.2: register trusted candidate-policy@1, publish SearchProgramTests, and verify durable reconstruction.
  • [x] M9.3: ship portable policy episodes, explicit splits, captured inner run references, exact reuse/resume boundaries, and nested usage separation.
  • [x] M9.4: aggregate all outcomes and strictly compare separate seed-only held-out outer runs without granting promotion authority.
  • [x] M9.5: run the deterministic durable flagship with development quality 6.0 → 7.0 → 8.0 and held-out aggregate 13.5 → 15.5.

docs.title: M9.0 executable contract
docs.text:
• meta_evolve.policy owns artifact-domain values; meta_evolve.policies continues to own executable presets.
  • Only generic MutationApplication[SurfaceT] and MutationSurface[MutationT, SurfaceT] move to meta_evolve.mutation; harness-specific mutations and parameters stay namespaced under harness.
  • Policy episodes and comparisons remain domain-specific peers of harness equivalents. No generic episode/comparison framework exists without a third domain demonstrating it.
  • An episode's existing content-addressed RunId is its sole cache identity. Aggregates are recomputed; evaluator identity covers the exact suite, split, scoring, aggregation, budgets, and environment.
  • Fresh development forbids non-identical reuse, while an exact completed run may reopen. Held-out execution always uses a new empty namespace and bypasses reuse.
  • Any failed, incomplete, or missing episode makes the aggregate non-rankable while retaining partial results and typed failures.
  • Inner trials and evaluations remain inner usage. Only tokens, monetary spend, and elapsed time roll into the enclosing evaluation's Usage.
  • Candidates cannot control tasks, seeds, proposers, evaluators, environments, budgets, split membership, caching, aggregation, promotion, or executable policy source.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Evaluate search or update policies as artifacts by measuring the improvement episodes they produce on held-out task distributions.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text: Two versioned PolicyArtifacts each control fresh inner-loop optimization episodes across training and held-out tasks. An outer policy compares their quality, cost, robustness, and failure rates under equal nested budgets.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• Serializable PolicyArtifact with declared interfaces and mutation boundaries.
  • Nested run/episode relationships and separate inner/outer budgets.
  • Task-distribution artifacts and held-out evaluation splits.
  • Existing RunId cache identity and explicit leakage boundaries.
  • Aggregation of quality, cost, uncertainty, and failure metrics across episodes.
  • External promotion decision for policy candidates.
  • examples/research/policy_evolution/.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• A policy candidate cannot inspect held-out results before its evaluation episode permits them.
  • Inner-loop events retain their own lineage while linking to the outer policy evaluation.
  • Cache hits are valid only when task, artifact, policy, evaluator, environment, seed, and relevant budget semantics match.
  • Promotion uses fresh evidence across multiple tasks or seeds rather than a policy's self-report.
  • Budget exhaustion in an inner episode does not consume undeclared outer authority.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Compare two deterministic policy artifacts across several task fixtures.
  • Nested budget accounting and exhaustion.
  • Held-out leakage rejection.
  • Cache-key correctness and invalidation.
  • Episode aggregation with failed and incomplete runs.
  • Replay from an outer decision to every supporting inner evaluation.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Learned schedulers, model-weight training inside the kernel, autonomous authority changes, production deployment, and claims that improvement generalizes beyond measured tasks.

docs.title: Milestone 9.5: advanced search
docs.text: Status: Shipped (August 17, 2026; #144, #148). M9.5 adds a bounded advanced-search slice after shipped M9, now that the M8 closure gate has passed. Its M9.5.1 archive-compatibility prerequisite, M9.5.2 specialist-retention slice, M9.5.3 tree-search slice, and M9.5.4 unified comparison are all complete. The local-author M10 does not depend on it; trusted distribution and federation move to M11 and M12. Tracked by #144. This interstitial milestone is distinct from M9's historical M9.5 executable substep, which assembled the already-shipped policy-evolution flagship.

docs.title: Ordered subissue program
docs.text:
• [x] #146 — M9.5.1: lock primary-objective defaults, frontier metric coverage, multi-member archive transitions, deterministic ties, named randomness, and history-derived policy statistics.
  • [x] #147 — M9.5.2: ship replayable per-key frontier evolution with deterministic winners, ownership-weighted parent selection, durable reconstruction, and focused equal-budget evidence.
  • [x] #145 — M9.5.3: ship replayable value-directed tree search with fixed progressive widening, best-descendant backup, durable reconstruction, and focused equal-budget evidence.
  • [x] #148 — M9.5.4: publish the deterministic equal-budget five-policy comparison after both concrete policies landed.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Demonstrate genuine multi-generation evolution through two concrete, replayable search policies: GEPA-style per-key frontier evolution and UCT-style tree allocation with best-descendant backup. Both must pass the existing search-program conformance suite and outperform the appropriate baseline on deterministic, equal-budget fixtures.

Specialists and TreeSearch are the shipped canonical names for per-metric specialist retention and value-directed tree allocation. Both use the policy namespace rather than adding a root export:

from meta_evolve.policies import Specialists, TreeSearch

Specialists(
    metrics=("case:0", "case:1", "case:2"),
    max_trials=20,
)

TreeSearch(
    max_trials=100,
    exploration=2**0.5,
)

BestOfN remains the one-generation equal-budget sampling control. M9.5 does not reopen the closed novelty, surrogate, or plateau-escalation proposals in #16, #17, or #18.

docs.title: Contract boundary
docs.text:
• Shipped default ranking, stopping, and incumbent selection use Task.objectives[0]; successful evaluations may retain additional metrics.
  • Specialists binds a fixed ordered metric-key tuple. Every successful candidate must contain each configured key; extra metrics are ignored and a missing key is invalid search history.
  • Archive membership remains authoritative. Existing records keep replaying; membership deltas may remove several members without a new schema version or removed_member_ids field. evicted_artifact_id is None for zero or multiple removals and identifies the member for exactly one removal.
  • Per-key winners, ownership weights, tree visits, subtree values, and normalization inputs reconstruct from durable history. M9.5 deliberately accepts derived-state recomputation cost instead of adding hidden caches.
  • Stable tie rules and named decision randomness make replay and cross-process reconstruction deterministic.
  • Failed evaluations remain typed outcomes: they never become frontier members or synthetic low tree rewards, though failed tree attempts still count as visits.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text:
M9.5.2 adds a focused deterministic scenario beside the existing scalar comparison: BestOfN, Population, and Specialists share the same task, seed, proposer, evaluator, root randomness, budget, and trial limit. Population evaluates then evicts an aggregate-weak per-case specialist; Specialists retains and expands it into the aggregate winner. The report pins score, lineage, parent sequence, evaluation and failure counts, and exact usage.

M9.5.3 adds a separate deterministic delayed-reward scenario: Greedy and TreeSearch share the same task, seed, proposer, evaluator, root randomness, budget, and explicit trial limit. Greedy's incumbent selection follows the immediately attractive branch to a plateau; TreeSearch's fixed widening also materializes the weaker delayed branch, and deterministic UCT descent revisits and expands it into the winner. The report pins score, lineage, parent sequence, evaluation and failure counts, and exact usage.

M9.5.4 adds one credential-free command, examples/learn/policy_comparison/advanced_search.py, that runs BestOfN, Greedy, Population, Specialists, and TreeSearch on both fixtures above under the same task, seed, proposer, evaluator, root randomness, budget, and explicit trial allowance, with equality verified pairwise through the existing Run.compare() gate. On the specialist fixture, capacity-matched Population evicts the aggregate-weak specialist that Specialists retains and expands into the aggregate winner 10, which equal-budget BestOfN never reaches. On the delayed-reward fixture, Greedy plateaus at the immediately attractive score 5 while TreeSearch revisits the weaker delayed branch and reaches its descendant 10. Every result's report pins primary score, lineage shape and depth, every selected parent, evaluation and failure counts, archive behavior, and exact resource usage; the other policy results stay visible without broadening either pair-specific claim.

Replay equivalence is a conformance invariant. The milestone's behavioral evidence is improvement on these controlled equal-budget fixtures.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Existing archive records replay, valid multi-removal transitions validate, and malformed membership deltas fail deterministically.
  • Frontier specialists remain selectable, one candidate may displace several obsolete members, missing dimensions fail, and extra dimensions are valid.
  • Frontier replay, resume, and cross-process reconstruction select identical parents.
  • Tree tests pin node selection, visit accounting, progressive widening, deterministic normalization, direction handling, and Q-value backup.
  • Failure-heavy tree branches remain representable without fabricated scores.
  • Both presets pass conformance, replay, and resume suites.
  • Both deterministic fixtures demonstrate the intended later-generation or delayed-reward advantage under equal budgets.
  • The unified five-policy comparison holds every external control equal within each fixture and reports complete structured evidence for every policy.
  • Examples, API references, guides, architecture, programming model, and implementation plan agreed before the status changed to Shipped.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Pareto archives, novelty search, islands, learned allocation, live-provider evidence, and extracting ParentSelector, Archive, BackupRule, or similar protocols. Revisit a shared protocol only after both concrete policies expose a repeated independently testable seam.

docs.title: Milestone 10: local author API and inspection experience
docs.text: Status: Shipped (August 14, 2026; #149). This milestone does not depend on M8.6 or M9.5.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Make local experiments easier to declare and pace, search algorithms easier to author, failures easier to diagnose, and artifact evolution easier to inspect. The public narrative is: proposers create candidates, evaluators judge them, search decides what to try next, and Meta-Evolve records the entire process. The subordinate M10.0 design record owns the six journey definitions, vocabulary decisions, and measured scorecard. The core remains dependency-free. An optional browser remains read-only and loopback-only, with no execution, resume, cancellation, promotion, deletion, remote collaboration, or distributed-operations authority.

docs.title: Ordered subissue program
docs.text:
• [x] #151 — M10.0: lock the local-author journeys, vocabulary, friction budget, compatibility promises, and bounded exception to the historical dashboard warning.
  • [x] #152 — M10.1: Shipped. An immutable typed Experiment declaration preserves the existing keyword-based run call and dictionary CLI compatibility through 1.x with a DeprecationWarning.
  • [x] #165 — M10.2: Shipped. The minimal improve() callable path lowers exactly through Task, Experiment, bounded Greedy, and local run().
  • [x] #164 — M10.3: Shipped. Functional incumbent refinement is available through a curated @meta.search façade over the full SearchProgram.next() protocol, with immutable identity-visible configuration and shared Greedy lowering.
  • [x] #153 — M10.4: Shipped. One immutable aggregate Run.inspect() read model covers complete, incomplete, rankable, and unrankable histories through exactly one authoritative validated replay.
  • [x] #154 — M10.5: Shipped. Genuinely read-only durable storage supports immutable inspection and exact per-run committed stream versions while observing live WAL commits.
  • [x] #166 — M10.6: Shipped. Paced and resumable Session execution is the sole synchronous dispatcher; run() and resume() exhaust it without changing durable history.
  • [x] #156 — M10.7: Shipped. An optional server-rendered local run browser uses only public inspection, comparison, read-only storage, and version APIs. One dedicated thread owns storage access; exact-version bounded caches avoid unnecessary replay; loopback-only routes expose no execution or mutation authority.
  • [x] #157 — M10.8: Shipped. Frozen-payload presentation, bounded direct-parent diffs, exact canonical attachments, occurrence-aware browser pages, optional custom-codec reconstruction, and the accessible visual system complete the read-only artifact history. Notebook HTML and screenshot automation belong to the explicit post-M10 presentation follow-up below.

The dependency order is:

M10.0 ─┬→ M10.1 → M10.2
       ├→ M10.3
       ├→ M10.4 ─┬→ M10.6 ← M10.1
       │          └→ M10.7 → M10.8
       └→ M10.5 ──────┘

Each child shipped through one focused PR.

docs.title: Acceptance gate
docs.text:
• M10.0 publishes the six measured journeys and decisions in the design record, meets both functional-search reduction thresholds, adds no proposed API, and preserves the uncreated examples/research/trusted_workers/ reservation.
  • Dictionary CLI factories remain supported through 1.x; M10.1 owns introducing the typed alternative and its DeprecationWarning.
  • Equivalent beginner, typed, keyword, and functional-search declarations retain the required honest identities and identical durable facts, decisions, stop reasons, and effective budgets where equivalence is claimed.
  • Functional search exposes only opaque seed/incumbent handles, immutable declared configuration, expand(), and stop(); captured configuration may not remain invisible to identity. Decision narration follows the #164 child contract.
  • One stable inspection view handles successful, failed, incomplete, and unrankable runs without winner-only assumptions. It exposes resolved defaults and immutable decision views reusable by paced execution.
  • Read-only storage performs no migration or filesystem mutation and exposes the maximum committed event sequence when supported.
  • Session fixes authority and budgets at start, commits and completes one decision per step, returns the committed terminal decision idempotently, and preserves byte-identical history across uninterrupted and resumed execution.
  • The optional browser imports only public inspection and storage APIs, polls versions before replay, binds only to loopback, and exposes no mutable or operational controls or imports of execution surfaces.
  • Occurrence identity remains distinct from content digest; artifact views and diffs never execute stored active content. Notebook HTML representations and screenshot automation belong to the post-M10 presentation follow-up.
  • Examples, public exports, tests, and canonical documentation match each surface before its status changes to Shipped.
  • The documentation entrance labels the scorecard as an authoring-friction measurement of proposed syntax, never optimization or runtime evidence.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Provider transcripts that were not durably recorded; remote or distributed dashboards; execution or governance controls; authentication claims; and frontier or tree presentation before M9.5 policies ship. Outer/inner loops, generations, and episodes remain relative explanatory terms rather than new core types. Deferred and rejected author surfaces are recorded once in the M10.0 design record.

docs.title: Post-M10 presentation follow-up
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. This follow-up owns notebook HTML representations built on the shipped inert presentation contract, plus browser screenshot automation or visual-regression evidence. It depends on the safe presentation boundary shipped in M10.8, is not part of the M10 closure gate, and adds no current notebook-rendering claim. Implementation requires its own future acceptance gate before either capability may be described as shipped.

docs.title: Issue #143 P1: monetary cost as a first-class resource
docs.text: Status: Shipped. Tracked by #143. First-class monetary usage: spend_micros in Usage/Budget and post-hoc enforcement. The field is absent at its default, so spend-free streams keep their existing bytes and the durable schema stays at v3 — a bump would have invalidated every stored pull-experience run, whose rendered text is byte-compared on replay. Issue #143 owns the requirements, and every acceptance criterion is recorded against the evidence that settles it. This work is independent of M11; M11's reservation and settlement deliverable is this work's P2, which adds the reservation-based hard cap that P1 deliberately omits.

docs.title: Milestone 11: trusted concurrency and distribution
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. Tracked by #10.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Execute work concurrently on trusted workers without corrupting history, budgets, population state, or promotion decisions.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text: Several worker processes claim bounded work through leases. Workers finish out of wall-clock order, one lease expires, and one result is submitted twice. The reconstructed logical run preserves one trial across delivery retries, contains one accepted outcome, and has correct budget accounting.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• Durable work states and atomic lease acquisition, renewal, expiration, cancellation, and completion.
  • WorkAttempt identities that remain distinct from their logical Trial and WorkItem.
  • Worker capability and resource declarations.
  • Idempotent result submission and retry policy.
  • Atomic budget reservation and settlement.
  • Scheduler matching work requirements to trusted workers.
  • Explicit consistency rules for durable facts, leases, heuristic frontier statistics, and promotion.
  • Multi-process load and fault-injection test harness.
  • examples/research/trusted_workers/.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• At most one completion has logical effect for an idempotency key.
  • Expired workers cannot overwrite an accepted result.
  • Out-of-order completion does not create future-information leakage.
  • Durable events and evaluations are strongly inserted; heuristic statistics may tolerate documented staleness.
  • Promotion and budget accounting use authoritative state.
  • Local and distributed runs preserve the same task, artifact, trial, work, evaluation, and event semantics.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Competing lease claims.
  • Lease renewal and expiration races.
  • Duplicate and late result submission.
  • Worker termination during execution and evaluation.
  • Atomic budget reservation under concurrency.
  • Projection rebuild after out-of-order events.
  • Load test with simulated trusted workers before paid agent fleets.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Arbitrary untrusted community code, Byzantine workers, public federation, reputation economies, and universal strong consistency.

docs.title: Milestone 12: contributed and federated network
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. Tracked by #11 and dependent on M11's trusted-worker boundary.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Allow independent installations to contribute and exchange authorized agents, evaluators, artifacts, evidence, and experience subgraphs with verifiable provenance.

docs.title: Canonical demonstration
docs.text: Two Meta-Evolve installations exchange a signed, policy-filtered experience bundle. The receiving installation verifies identity and content, imports only authorized records, preserves source provenance and restrictions, independently evaluates a promoted candidate, and processes a later retraction.

docs.title: Deliverables
docs.text:
• Signed manifests for contributors, agents, evaluators, tasks, environments, and artifact schemas.
  • Scoped identities and task-specific trust policies.
  • Canonical export/import format for policy-filtered experience subgraphs.
  • Verification of signatures, content digests, schema compatibility, causal closure, and access labels.
  • Provenance, licensing, embargo, attribution, and retraction propagation through derivation edges.
  • Independent or redundant evaluation for promotion-sensitive results.
  • Minimal dispute and reputation projections based on recorded evidence.
  • examples/research/federated_exchange/ using two local installations.

docs.title: Expected behavior
docs.text:
• Import never grants broader access than the source export policy and receiving trust policy allow.
  • Missing private ancestors can be represented by verifiable redacted references without fabricating lineage.
  • Invalid signatures, digests, schemas, or causal references are rejected.
  • Imported evaluations are evidence, not automatic local promotion.
  • Retractions and permission changes identify dependent artifacts, datasets, skills, and checkpoints.
  • Operators may keep private events while publishing permitted claims and artifacts.

docs.title: Acceptance tests
docs.text:
• Successful signed export/import between two installations.
  • Tampered payload, signature, digest, and causal-edge rejection.
  • Private, embargoed, and redacted source handling.
  • Conflicting evaluator results and independent verification.
  • Retraction propagation through derived records.
  • Duplicate import idempotency and schema-version negotiation.
  • Threat-model review covering code execution, evaluator collusion, poisoning, sybil behavior, reward hacking, and correlated replication.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text: Token economies, unrestricted peer-to-peer execution, global consensus, claims that containers alone secure untrusted code, and scientific validity without domain-governed evidence and replication.

docs.title: Architecture gate across all milestones
docs.text:
The following test should remain true throughout development:

new use case
  = artifact codec and schema
  + task and evaluator
  + agent or mutator
  + search/context configuration
  + optional infrastructure adapters

new use case
  ≠ coordinator branch
  ≠ new durable semantics
  ≠ bypassed authority boundary

When a new domain does not fit, first determine whether it needs a general protocol capability or whether it lies outside evaluated artifact-improvement loops. The kernel should grow only for the former.

docs.title: Operations and extensions
docs.text:
Status: Shipped.

Start with two runs in one durable store:

uv run meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/experiment.py --storage ./store
uv run meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/best_of_n.py --storage ./store
uv run meta-evolve list --storage ./store

run imports one side-effect-free experiment() factory returning meta.Experiment and prints the new run's summary. list returns the stored run IDs. Use those IDs next:

uv run meta-evolve inspect <greedy-run-id> --storage ./store
uv run meta-evolve compare <greedy-run-id> <best-of-n-run-id> --storage ./store

inspect reports one summary, lineage, and best artifact. compare first checks that the task, initial artifact, budget, and proposer declarations are compatible. It then reports both runs and their winner. The BestOfN module reuses the first module's declarations so only search behavior changes.

For an optional server-rendered view over the same read-only public queries:

uv sync --extra browser
uv run meta-evolve ui --storage ./store --port 8000

The local browser guide documents its fixed loopback scope, exact-version caches, rendering exclusions, and absence of authentication.

The canonical examples/operations/command_line/ walkthrough pins this entire transcript through subprocess tests.

docs.title: Resume is a declared capability
docs.text:
Create a reconstructable run, then resume it:

uv run meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/resumable.py \
    --storage ./store --mode durable-local
uv run meta-evolve resume <run-id> \
    --module examples/operations/command_line/resumable.py --storage ./store

The module registers source-digestible proposer and evaluator functions. On resume, its factory rebuilds the registry and the library verifies the recorded component identities. A local run may use durable storage and remains listable and inspectable, but it is not resumable.

The command line adds no capability rules. It passes --mode to meta.run and lets meta.resume accept or refuse the recorded run. The CLI and browser guide owns the five report-verb mappings, factory convention, modes, and exit codes.

For a real interrupted-process workflow, continue with the examples/operations/durable_operations/ walkthrough.

docs.title: Add a local artifact domain
docs.text:
The add-a-domain tutorial builds and executes a Recipe value, codec, registration, task, proposer, and evaluator. Its custom codec runs through the published codec suite.

That codec is a live Python object. It has no durable component manifest. In M9, mode="durable-local" therefore accepts only the six built-in (kind, representation) keys and rejects a registered custom codec before writing events. There is no silent fallback to local execution.

A custom-domain local run may still write to Storage.durable(...). After a restart, rebuild the same registry and open it through meta.Run(run_id, storage, registry=registry). This grants decoding authority only. It does not make the run resumable.

The CLI cannot perform that reopening. inspect and compare accept no registry argument, so they can decode built-in domains only. Use Python for a stored custom domain. This is a reconstruction limit, not a codec or storage failure.

docs.title: Conformance: every extension component family
docs.text:
Install the opt-in test extra before importing the published suites:

uv sync --extra conformance

meta_evolve.conformance publishes a reusable suite for each of the seven extension component families, plus the typed mutation-surface contract that M8 and M9 grew:

Component family Reusable coverage today Artifact codecs Published ArtifactCodecTests Repository-editing proposers Published RepositoryProposerTests and PullRepositoryProposerTests; exercised by in-repo reference callables Evaluators Published EvaluatorTests Search programs Published SearchProgramTests; Greedy, BestOfN, BestOfK, Population, CandidatePolicy, and a next-only custom program Context policies Published ContextPolicyTests Workspaces Published WorkspaceProviderTests Sandboxes Published SandboxProviderTests; cwd/environment/argv/streams, timeout, independent byte bounds, partial output, and wall-only usage Typed mutation surfaces Published MutationSurfaceTests; four built-in implementations

Store adapters keep an internal tests/store_contract.py. It is not one of those extension families and is not published from meta_evolve.conformance.

Published means an extension author can subclass the suite from an installed package. Internal means repository tests reuse assertions that are not part of the installed extension surface. Every published suite is subclassed inside tests/ — the built-ins where they exist, and in-repository reference callables for the two proposer suites, whose first-party provider adapters were replaced by the user-owned SDK boundary (no provider adapter ships). The published-conformance section of the extensions guide owns suite contents and limitations. Its migration section shows the required pre-1.0 codec and mutation-surface fixture updates.

A published suite states what it does not check as carefully as what it does. EvaluatorTests skips its typed-failure law, visibly, when a subclass declares no rejected_candidates; ArtifactCodecTests does the same for its aliasing law when mutable_values is (); ContextPolicyTests excludes NoMemory, which meta.run normalizes away before any policy runs, and asks a policy that selects nothing to declare it through expects_records rather than pass in silence.

One law is easy to think redundant and is not. EvaluatorTests checks that scoring does not edit the candidate. With the built-in codecs an evaluator only ever sees a frozen value decoded from the stored payload, so it cannot reach the caller's object — but a codec is user-supplied, and one that returns the instance it was handed gives the evaluator the real thing.

ArtifactCodecTests.mutable_values is how you say which of your values can be modified in place; the codec suite then checks — through your value_state and mutate methods, never through the codec's own encode — that decode hands back an independent object. Every value comparison in the suite goes through value_state rather than the value type's __eq__, and rejected_payloads demands the decode-side refusals that make "decode is validation" true. It has no default, like rejected_values — () is a positive claim that your values are immutable, not a way to skip the question. The law cannot simply apply to everything, because the built-in python-value codec decodes a small integer to the very same interned object and that is harmless. So the two suites cover the same failure from both ends: the codec law where the leak starts, the evaluator law where it does damage.

docs.title: Lab questions
docs.text:
1. Why can a local custom-domain run survive on disk but still require the live registry to decode after restart?
  2. Which CLI verb first makes an interrupted run reachable when its ID never reached terminal output?
  3. If you implement a search program that has to be built around the proposer, which of SearchProgramTests' two fixtures do you override, and why can the other one not express it?

Continue to the optional, paid bounded live-agent track only when you can authenticate both providers and accept up to 12 calls.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Status: Shipped. This page owns the public execution contracts. The generated API reference owns exact signatures; task-focused pages own recipes. M8, M8.7, M9/9.5, M10, and monetary P1 are shipped. M11, M12, and the post-M10 presentation follow-up are Design—not shipped.

docs.title: The smallest complete job
docs.text:
import meta_evolve as meta

result = meta.improve(
    seed="draft",
    proposer=revise,
    evaluator=grade,
    trials=3,
)

The seed is an evaluated baseline. The proposer creates successors. The independent evaluator measures valid candidates. trials bounds successor attempts, excluding the seed. improve() lowers to the ordinary Task → Experiment → bounded Greedy → run() path; it has no separate execution or durable identity.

docs.title: Expanded declarations
docs.text:
task = meta.Task(
    evaluator=grade,
    objectives=(meta.Maximize("quality", satisfy=1.0),),
    budget=meta.Budget(evaluations=9, trials=8),
)
experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=task,
    seed="draft",
    proposer=revise,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=8),
    random_seed=0,
)
result = meta.run(experiment)

Use the expanded form for typed artifacts, named objectives, search, context, experience, durable execution, or registered components. Experiment is an immutable declaration. Storage, mode, and a narrowing run budget are execution overlays, not declaration fields. The source-compatible keyword form of run() lowers through the same declaration and remains available through 1.x.

docs.title: Callable contracts
docs.text:
A proposer receives a decoded parent and may also request ProposerContext. It returns a candidate or ProposalResult. A rich result may carry evidence, metadata, usage, and authorized derivation references.

An evaluator receives the candidate outside candidate authority. It returns a scalar, a metric mapping, EvaluationResult, or a typed failure. Trial and evaluation counts are coordinator-owned. Tokens, charged spend_micros, and elapsed time may be reported by wrappers. See What evaluation may return and Connect an agent or model.

CapabilityError states a fact about missing configuration or machine capability and aborts the run. It must not be raised conditionally for one poor candidate. Candidate-specific invalid output, proposer/evaluator faults, timeouts, exhaustion, and policy violations remain recorded typed outcomes and are never converted to low scores.

docs.title: Results and comparison
docs.text:
Run is a read-only handle over committed facts:

  • best() and best_trial() query a rankable winner;
  • trials() and inspect() work for failed or incomplete histories;
  • lineage() follows causal artifact occurrences;
  • summary() exposes portable score, usage, and identity;
  • compare() refuses incompatible measuring conditions.

No query reruns a proposer, evaluator, context selector, or provider. Selecting a winner never deploys it. See What a run returns and What a comparison may claim.

docs.title: Search
docs.text: Search chooses which occurrence to expand and when to stop. It cannot evaluate, mutate, or widen budgets. Shipped presets are Greedy, BestOfN, BestOfK, Population, Specialists, and TreeSearch. @search adapts a bounded seed/incumbent rule; archive- or population-shaped actions stay on SearchProgram.next(). Routing and current preset behavior live in Choose search; the full seam lives in Custom search.

docs.title: Context and experience
docs.text:
Experience is off by default. A context policy may push a bounded committed bundle. PullAccess may grant a scoped, audited ExperienceReader. Proposal derivation may cite only successful authorized observations.

M8.7 adds bounded listing and reads of exact prior source occurrences, canonical source diffs, and an optional disposable Git presentation. It does not grant ambient repository, cross-run, semantic-search, or persistent Git authority. See Experience and derivation and the M8.7 contract.

docs.title: Artifacts and external execution
docs.text:
Built-in values include text, immutable UTF-8 source trees, skill sets, agent harnesses, and search-policy artifacts. Custom kinds enter through registered codecs; the coordinator never branches on a kind.

Repository-style proposers work from an immutable parent in a private mutable workspace and return one immutable successor. Evaluators materialize candidates in fresh workspaces and own hidden graders, commands, environments, and failure translation. Milestone 5 is complete; the canonical code-repair job demonstrates the current source boundary.

docs.title: Execution, durability, and presentation
docs.text:
local accepts live Python components and defaults to memory storage. Persisting a local run preserves inspection history but does not promise cold reconstruction. durable-local requires durable storage plus registered, reconstructible components.

Session.start() and Session.resume() expose paced execution; run() and resume() exhaust that same dispatcher. Authority and effective budget are fixed at start. Replay projects committed facts and performs no external work. Storage.read_only() grants inspection, not migration or execution. The optional browser is loopback-only and read-only. See Persist and resume and Use the CLI and browser.

docs.title: Nested evaluated loops
docs.text: The constructible harness family lives under meta_evolve.harness; policy artifacts live under meta_evolve.policy. Their evaluators may run isolated inner experiments, but inner trial/evaluation counts remain inner usage. Only tokens, charged spend, and elapsed time roll up when explicitly captured. Held-out comparison reports promotion eligibility and grants no promotion authority. See Harness evolution and Policy evolution.

docs.title: Public routing
docs.text:
Need Owner Exact types and signatures API reference Evaluators and failures Evaluation outcomes Usage and monetary limits Bound cost Search presets Choose search Experience and source inspection Experience Extension protocols Extensions Shipped semantics Architecture Sequence and status Milestones

The simplicity test remains: a common job fits improve(seed, proposer, evaluator, trials); a common expansion is one Task, one Experiment, and one run(experiment).

docs.title: Research and Systems References
docs.text:
This is a working map of neighboring ideas. Meta-Evolve should implement, compose, and compare these approaches rather than rename one of them as a universal solution. For a plain-language comparison with AlphaEvolve and GEPA's optimize_anything, see How Meta-Evolve compares.

Claims about capabilities in these papers belong to the cited systems. Their inclusion here does not mean Meta-Evolve has reproduced their results.

docs.title: Experience Graphs / Trellis
docs.text:
Experience Graphs: The Data Foundation for Self-Improving Agents treats the causal state produced by long-horizon search—attempts, executable artifacts, prompts, tool outputs, rewards, siblings, search statistics, and lineage—as governed database state.

Important implications for Meta-Evolve:

  • stateless agents can recover and collaborate through durable shared experience;
  • online search, causal traversal, semantic reuse, temporal reconstruction, observability, and training views operate over one logical model;
  • the system must preserve the state observed when a decision was made, not only final mutated search statistics;
  • experience retrieval is a policy with an exploration-versus-anchoring tradeoff;
  • derived skills and training views inherit provenance and access constraints.

The paper reports preliminary domain-specific results for cross-session reuse in kernel optimization, including faster early convergence and fewer buggy nodes, while aggressive reuse reduced strategy diversity and missed the best final candidate. This motivates controlled context-policy experiments rather than a general claim that more memory always improves search.

Trellis overlaps with Meta-Evolve's data plane, not its entire product scope. Meta-Evolve focuses additionally on programmable harness and search abstractions, execution adapters, contributed agents/evaluators/compute, verification, and federation.

docs.title: DSPy
docs.text:
DSPy provides a declarative programming model for modular LM programs and optimizers that compile prompts and demonstrations against metrics.

Meta-Evolve should integrate DSPy in both directions:

  • wrap a DSPy program as a versioned harness component;
  • use a DSPy optimizer for an inner prompt/program compilation loop;
  • expose Meta-Evolve examples and evaluators as DSPy-compatible data and metrics;
  • capture compiled programs as immutable artifacts;
  • let an outer Meta-Evolve policy compare DSPy with other optimizers.

The boundary is: DSPy programs LM pipelines; Meta-Evolve programs and evolves populations of executable systems, including DSPy pipelines.

docs.title: GEPA
docs.text: GEPA uses reflective textual mutation and Pareto selection to optimize LM components from task feedback. It is a reference for TextArtifact mutation, evidence-aware reflection, and Pareto retention.

docs.title: Feedback Descent
docs.text: Feedback Descent motivates structured comparison feedback followed by feedback-derived prompt edits. The research lab isolates that mechanism without claiming to reproduce its results.

docs.title: AutoData
docs.text: AutoData motivates evolving data-generation recipes with solver-based quality signals. The local lab's same-model/different-context restricted/informed setup is explicitly a teaching simplification and confounder.

docs.title: EvoSkill
docs.text: EvoSkill motivates failure-driven discovery, consolidation, and held-out selection of reusable skills. Meta-Evolve should express this as evolution of SkillArtifact and SkillSetArtifact objects rather than a special memory subsystem.

docs.title: Meta-Harness
docs.text:
Meta-Harness moves optimization beyond prompts to the source code and control logic surrounding a fixed model. It motivates HarnessArtifact, typed mutation surfaces, full execution history, and external authority boundaries.

Its agentic proposer can selectively inspect the source, scores, and execution traces of prior candidates through a filesystem instead of receiving only compressed feedback. Meta-Evolve should preserve this agent-directed exploration as a scoped ExperienceReader capability alongside policy-pushed context. A read-only filesystem projection can provide compatibility for coding agents, while structured graph tools add causal traversal, logical-time queries, provenance, and governance.

docs.title: Shepherd
docs.text:
Shepherd is a runtime substrate that records an agent's model actions, tool calls, and environment changes as a reversible, forkable execution trace. Its unit of control is an execution in progress; Meta-Evolve's unit of evolution is an immutable artifact evaluated between trials. The two models are therefore adjacent rather than interchangeable.

A useful composition would keep Meta-Evolve in charge of tasks, search, budgets, independent evaluation, lineage, and promotion while a user-owned Shepherd-backed proposer supplies isolated execution, retained workspace output, and trace-level evidence. Any such integration should begin as an external adapter experiment: the captured artifact remains durable truth, trace references are supporting evidence, and restored or forked execution must not bypass trial or usage accounting. Shepherd's visual-artifact notebooks are also a useful teaching reference for deterministic-first examples, optional live runs, and progressive disclosure of execution internals.

docs.title: Asari inference-stack optimization
docs.text:
Asari's inference-optimization report describes many agents improving a pinned vLLM serving stack through a discover/build, evaluate, verify, and self-improve loop. It reports changes across kernels, schedulers, load balancing, and configuration, using hierarchical performance benchmarks, measurement-noise controls, and token-distribution correctness checks.

A bounded Meta-Evolve version maps cleanly onto current seams:

  • a small SourceTree overlay holds candidate kernel and configuration edits;
  • a user-owned SDK proposer investigates and changes that overlay;
  • a custom evaluator builds it against an evaluator-owned base, verifies model behavior, and returns performance metrics, uncertainty, evidence, and usage;
  • context or audited experience exposes earlier profiler and failure evidence;
  • search retains alternatives while lineage records which evidence informed each change; and
  • an external decision, never the candidate, owns production promotion.

The shipped CommandEvaluator is only a binary, single-metric exit-code adapter, so a trustworthy experiment needs a domain evaluator that parses repeated benchmark samples. A local sequential precursor is feasible, but a whole-stack implementation also needs typed mutation surfaces and portable episodes from M8 and M9, plus trusted parallel GPU workers from M11. Cross-run knowledge transfer must be introduced explicitly rather than silently widening M3's same-run experience boundary.

Meta-Evolve does not reproduce Asari's results. The scoped future work is tracked in issue #118: start with one kernel on one trusted GPU, preserve null and negative results, and defer many-agent whole-stack optimization until its dependencies ship.

docs.title: AIDE²
docs.text: Weco's AIDE² report describes a bi-level experiment in which an outer autoresearch loop rewrites an inner research agent, evaluates each rewrite across heterogeneous tasks under a fixed cost, and selects using private scores. Its reported empirical claims belong to that system. Meta-Evolve's autoresearch teaching example demonstrates only the small nested-run, budget, evidence, and split boundaries; it is not a reproduction or evidence of recursive self-improvement.

docs.title: AlphaEvolve
docs.text: AlphaEvolve demonstrates coding-agent-driven evolutionary search for algorithmic and scientific problems. It is a reference for program artifacts, evaluator-guided evolution, and populations of executable candidates.

docs.title: FunSearch
docs.text: FunSearch combines LLM-generated programs with automated evaluation and evolutionary selection for mathematical discovery. It illustrates why executable artifacts and objective evaluators are powerful while also showing that the evaluator and representation bound the discovery process.

docs.title: OpenEvolve
docs.text: OpenEvolve is an open evolutionary coding-agent framework and useful implementation reference for program databases, evaluation, and search loops. Meta-Evolve should seek adapter compatibility where practical rather than duplicate APIs without benefit.

docs.title: EvoX
docs.text: EvoX motivates treating both solutions and the search strategy as evolving artifacts. This corresponds to nested task evaluation of PolicyArtifact and SearchProgram candidates.

docs.title: Group-Evolving Agents
docs.text: Group-Evolving Agents studies evolution at the level of composite agent groups and shared experience. It is relevant to TopologyArtifact, performance-novelty selection, and group-level mutation.

docs.title: Agent0 and Dr. Zero
docs.text: Agent0 and Dr. Zero explore proposer-solver co-evolution and self-generated curricula under verifiable rewards. They motivate explicit curriculum, checkpoint, training-job, and evaluator artifacts with separate validation boundaries.

docs.title: AERO
docs.text: AERO couples self-questioning, answering, criticism, and iterative model updates. It is relevant to synthetic-experience artifacts and external training loops consuming experience-graph views.

docs.title: CORAL
docs.text: CORAL is relevant to parallel coding agents, evaluated repository successors, shared knowledge, islands, and migration. In Meta-Evolve this becomes one GitTreeArtifact task configuration rather than the universal runtime model.

docs.title: Quality diversity and island models
docs.text: Quality-diversity methods, novelty search, MAP-Elites, Pareto archives, and island models are important baselines for maintaining heterogeneous strategies and avoiding premature convergence. They should be implemented as replaceable population and migration policies.

docs.title: MemGPT
docs.text: MemGPT frames agent memory as a hierarchy that moves information between limited context and external storage. Meta-Evolve's ContextPolicy operates at this transport boundary, while the experience graph defines durable causal search state beneath it.

docs.title: Graphiti and structured memory
docs.text: Graphiti is relevant to temporal knowledge graphs and dynamic synthesis of agent memory. Meta-Evolve additionally needs executable artifacts, objective rewards, search-policy state, training views, and causal sibling/path queries.

docs.title: Event sourcing and content addressing
docs.text:
Event sourcing, temporal databases, MVCC/change-data capture, content-addressed storage, reproducible build systems, and scientific provenance systems provide established foundations for immutable facts, current projections, time travel, lineage, deduplication, and audit.

Meta-Evolve should reuse conventional database and storage systems until its measured workload demonstrates a need for specialized physical design.

docs.title: Research questions for Meta-Evolve
docs.text:
• When does heterogeneous agent diversity improve compute-normalized progress?
  • Which context policies accelerate reuse without suppressing novelty?
  • Which topologies and migration policies avoid premature convergence?
  • How should compute be allocated among exploration, exploitation, repair, synthesis, and replication?
  • Which graph features predict the value of expanding or abandoning a branch?
  • How do skills and discoveries transfer across models, harnesses, tasks, and domains?
  • Which consistency guarantees are sufficient for concurrent search?
  • How should access changes and retractions propagate into derived skills, datasets, and checkpoints?
  • Can learned or evolved search policies generalize to held-out task distributions?
  • When do nested improvement loops plateau, destabilize, or exploit evaluators?
  • What evidence and replication policies predict real scientific validity?

docs.title: SealQA research labs
docs.text: Status: Experimental/live-only. These are small teaching mechanisms, not paper reproductions or an official SealQA evaluation. The complete curriculum contains at most 24 sessions.

docs.title: Where the notebooks are
docs.text: The four unexecuted notebooks live under examples/research/sealqa_labs/ and are published byte-for-byte under docs/notebooks/18_sealqa_research_labs/. Standalone chapters explain Feedback Descent, AutoData, the pre-M8 harness precursor, and EvoSkill.

docs.title: The common experimental substrate
docs.text: All labs consume a structural SessionRunner. The repository supplies orchestration and deterministic injected-runner tests; users supply any live SDK wrapper. The wrapper owns authentication, structured decoding, tools, permissions, model configuration, and provider telemetry.

docs.title: What is frozen and what may change
docs.text: The fixture questions, documents, evaluator-only answers, schemas, session arithmetic, and mutation allowlists are frozen. Candidate prompts, recipes, permitted harness files, and skills may change. The wrapper declaration and all behavior-affecting configuration must be recorded before a live run.

docs.title: Leakage boundary
docs.text: Solver views contain only public document ids, titles, dates, and text. Gold answers, source URLs, split roles, evaluation rules, permissions, budgets, and promotion decisions remain outside candidate authority.

docs.title: Failure and scoring semantics
docs.text: Malformed structured output, missing candidates, timeout, exhaustion, SDK or infrastructure failure, and protected-control edits are typed and unrankable. They are never converted into a low score. Deterministic graders alone produce rankable measurements.

docs.title: Evidence, lineage, and identity
docs.text: Each session retains its label, decoded value or typed failure, wrapper evidence, token and elapsed usage, and experience counters. Derived artifacts name their source evidence. A wrapper configuration change changes declared identity and prevents uncontrolled comparison.

docs.title: How the shared components actually work
docs.text: UserSdkSessionRunner invokes a user-provided proposer inside an ordinary one-trial meta.run(). A successful wrapper returns ProposalResult, puts the schema-decoded value in sdk.structured-output evidence, and reports only shared token and elapsed usage. The lab validates that value again before using it.

docs.title: How to run the curriculum
docs.text:
Create an opt-in driver outside the shipped examples. Implement build_agent(request), identify its declaration, and pass it to UserSdkSessionRunner; then call run_selected. Review the maximum call count, SDK permissions, and spending limits before setting META_EVOLVE_LIVE_SDK=1.

No official provider capture is pending. Users may perform one authorized run with their own wrapper. Any published capture must identify the wrapper declaration and preserve ties, failures, null results, and regressions honestly. The notebooks contain illustrative code and no fabricated live output.

docs.title: Keep authority where it belongs
docs.text:
Status: Shipped.

A proposer can claim anything — a confident claim is not a measurement. Meta-Evolve survives unreliable proposers because every field in a run has exactly one owner. Your first evolution demonstrates the separation; this page names it.

docs.title: Three fields, three owners
docs.text:
A trial's record splits into three kinds of fields:

  • Candidate-controlled — the proposed artifact content and its declared citations. Everything a proposer decides, and nothing else.
  • Experiment-controlled — the task, evaluator, hidden data, environment, seeds, and budgets. The evaluator scores independently; a proposer's claim about its own quality never moves a metric.
  • Governance-controlled — permissions, admission, visibility, and promotion. These live outside the run entirely.
candidate            experiment             governance
─────────            ──────────             ──────────
artifact content     evaluator + data       permissions
declared citations   budgets + seeds        visibility
                     environments           promotion

A candidate cannot read or edit the grader, enlarge its budget, erase a failure, or grant itself permissions. Those controls stay with the experiment and its operator.

Audited source inspection applies the same boundary to history: a proposer can receive only the bounded observations granted to it, while verification and presentation stay outside candidate authority. The full shipped boundary is owned by the M8.7 contract.

docs.title: Proposal is not promotion
docs.text:
Search may select a best measured artifact. That selection grants no production authority: promotion — actually deploying the selected artifact — is an external governance act that no candidate and no search policy can perform. A run ends with a recommendation and its evidence, never with a deployment. The harness- and policy-evolution examples print this boundary explicitly (promotion=external); see the harness evolution guide.

The authority invariants are canonical in the architecture and are not restated here.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
Make a proposer attach a glowing self-assessment to its proposal metadata. Predict metrics identical to the same candidate without the self-praise: metadata is candidate-controlled, measurement is not.

Previous: Trust a shipped contract · Next: Fail with a type, not a zero

docs.title: Trust a shipped contract
docs.text:
Status: Shipped.

You wrote a custom evaluator, codec, or search program. How do you know it obeys the same rules the built-in components obey? You run the same published tests the library runs on itself.

docs.title: What a conformance suite is
docs.text:
meta_evolve.conformance publishes one pytest-native suite per extension component family. Each suite is a plain class of laws whose collaborators arrive as fixtures: subclass it, name the subclass Test... so pytest collects it, override the fixtures with your component, and the laws run against your implementation.

published suite               your test module
───────────────               ────────────────
ArtifactCodecTests      <--   class TestMyCodec(ArtifactCodecTests):
  law: decode(encode(v))          fixture: my codec
  law: decode is validation       fixture: rejected payloads
  law: no aliasing                fixture: mutable values

The suites install through an explicit extra, so using the library never pulls in a test runner:

uv sync --extra conformance

docs.title: What the library proves about itself
docs.text:
Every published suite is subclassed inside the repository's own tests, so the built-in codecs, evaluators, policies, and search programs pass exactly the laws an extension author receives. A suite also states what it does not check as carefully as what it does: EvaluatorTests skips its typed-failure law, visibly, when a subclass declares no rejected candidates, and ArtifactCodecTests does the same for its aliasing law. Silence is never counted as passing.

One law is easy to think redundant and is not: EvaluatorTests checks that scoring does not edit the candidate. With built-in codecs an evaluator only ever sees a frozen decoded value — but a custom codec that returns the instance it was handed gives the evaluator the real thing, so the law waits where the damage would land.

docs.title: When you reach for one
docs.text:
• You registered an artifact domain — run your codec through ArtifactCodecTests, as Add an artifact domain does in its final step.
  • You wrote an evaluator, context policy, workspace, sandbox, search program, or repository proposer — the operations lab lists every family and its published suite.

Suite contents and deliberate limitations are canonical in the extensions guide and are not restated here.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
Subclass ArtifactCodecTests around a codec whose decode returns the exact instance it was handed, and declare one mutable value. Predict a named aliasing-law failure, not a vague error: the suite tells you which contract your codec broke.

Previous: Attach evidence to results · Next: Keep authority where it belongs

docs.title: Encode any artifact
docs.text:
Status: Shipped.

The loop never inspects what it improves. A number, a prompt, a repository, a harness — every artifact travels as a typed payload that one registered codec translates, so no coordinator code branches on what you evolve.

docs.title: Six built-in kinds
docs.text:
Every artifact is stored under a (kind, representation) key. Six keys ship built in:

Kind Representation What it holds python-value canonical-json any canonically serializable value — the default text utf8-text-v1 one UTF-8 document: a prompt, a config, an essay source-tree utf8-tree-v1 an immutable directory of UTF-8 files skill-set utf8-tree-v1 named skill documents agent-harness harness-manifest-v1 a portable agent-harness bundle search-policy policy-manifest-v1 declarative search-policy values

Text optimization and skill evolution run two of these through the identical meta.run call site; SQL migrations registers a seventh, custom domain and is the runnable tour of everything on this page.

docs.title: Kind versus representation
docs.text: The kind, never the bytes, decides which codec reads a committed payload. source-tree and skill-set share the same tree bytes (utf8-tree-v1) and still decode differently, because a payload's meaning is a declared contract rather than an inference from its shape.

docs.title: Why custom domains stay durable-local
docs.text:
A registered custom codec is a live Python object with no verifiable manifest. A durable run must be reopenable by a reader who can decode every payload from the record alone — a payload another machine cannot decode is not shareable evidence. So durable-local mode accepts only the six built-in keys and rejects a custom codec before writing any event, with no silent fallback. A local run with a custom domain still works and may still write durable storage; reopening it later means rebuilding the same registry in Python, which grants decoding, not resumption.

To build a domain end to end, follow Add an artifact domain. Codec laws are canonical in the programming model and the published conformance suite, and are not restated here.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
Seed a text task with a tuple instead of a string. Predict a typed refusal at ingress — utf8-text-v1 tasks require a str value — before any trial runs: decode and encode are validation, not best-effort coercion.

Previous: Count the work exactly · Build one: Add an artifact domain

docs.title: Attach evidence to results
docs.text:
Status: Shipped.

A score says how good a candidate measured. Evidence says what was actually observed on the way to that measurement — and who observed it. Three different authorities can attach evidence to one run, and they never blur.

uv run python examples/learn/experience_reuse/evidence_story.py
Output
seed evidence: ('grader-transcript',)
successor evidence: ('hypothesis-note', 'grader-transcript')
last proposal derived from: 3 prior records
audited pull: operations=6 records=8

docs.title: 1. Evidence on an evaluation
docs.text: The evaluator returns an EvaluationResult that carries an EvidenceDraft beside its metrics. The seed trial shows only grader-transcript: evaluator-authored evidence of what the grader observed. Evidence records what was observed; it is not a candidate-controlled score.

docs.title: 2. Evidence on a proposal
docs.text: The proposer returns a ProposalResult with a draft of its own. The successor trial adds hypothesis-note: candidate-authored evidence stating the claim behind the change. A proposer can write anything here, and its score does not move — the metrics stay with the independent evaluator.

docs.title: 3. Evidence a later candidate can read
docs.text:
With PullAccess, a later proposal searches prior evidence records and opens the ones it uses. The last proposal cited three: the seed's grader transcript plus both records from the first successor. Every read is audited — six operations and eight returned records are charged and inspectable — and the citations land in the trial's derived_from edges.

This page is about evidence records inside a run. The Evidence notebooks navigation section is different: it holds the captured notebook companions to the Learn chapters.

Evidence fields and authority are canonical in the programming model and architecture and are not restated here.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
Remove the hypothesis-note draft from the proposer. Predict the successor line shrinking to ('grader-transcript',) while derived_from still cites two prior records: the proposal's citations never depended on the proposal publishing evidence of its own.

Previous: Tell equal bytes apart · Next: Trust a shipped contract

docs.title: Tell equal bytes apart
docs.text:
Status: Shipped.

A proposer can hand back a value byte-identical to one the run has already seen. Are they the same artifact? Meta-Evolve answers with two identities: one for the bytes, one for the causal event that produced them.

uv run python examples/learn/checklist/_stories/identity_story.py
Output
seed: id=f953e1f8 digest=6ae048f0 parents=()
successor: id=227a6a34 digest=6ae048f0 parents=('f953e1f8',)
successor: id=99877b49 digest=6ae048f0 parents=('f953e1f8',)
content digests equal: True
distinct occurrence ids: 3

The proposer restates its parent unchanged, twice, under BestOfN. Three artifacts hold the same five bytes. The run still records three distinct things.

docs.title: Content identity is the bytes
docs.text: The digest is a stable hash of the encoded artifact value. All three rows share 6ae048f0 because all three values are "draft". Equal bytes always produce an equal digest, so storage deduplicates payloads and a transcript of digests stays stable across reruns. The lineage: ('659bfe4a', '08abe248') line in Repair code with an agent demonstrates this: a digest prefix for each lineage step.

docs.title: Occurrence identity is the causal event
docs.text:
The occurrence id names one appearance of those bytes at one position in the run: proposed from which parents, at which logical step. The seed has no parents. Each successor names the seed as its parent and receives its own id. Equal artifact bytes in different causal positions remain different occurrences.

This distinction is also why audited source inspection authorizes an exact prior occurrence rather than matching content alone. The shipped contract and its storage edge are owned by M8.7.2–M8.7.3.

docs.title: Why the run needs both
docs.text:
Two trials that produce byte-identical artifacts remain different causal events: they may have different parents, observations, usage, and failures. Collapsing them would erase which attempt actually earned its evaluation. Replay and audited experience address records by causal position, never by content, so history stays exact even when values repeat. The experience lesson shows the same rule inside the temporal graph.

Both identities are canonical in the architecture and are not restated here.

docs.title: Change and predict
docs.text:
Change restate to return parent + "!". Predict digests that stop being equal while the parent links stay exactly the same: content identity follows the bytes; occurrence identity never depended on them.

Examples · Next: Attach evidence to results

docs.text:

This directory contains proposals for behavior beyond the current milestone. Design pages are subordinate to the canonical shipped public API contract, shipped architecture contract, and the acceptance boundary in the milestone roadmap. Use these status labels throughout the documentation:

Status Meaning Shipped Available in the current package and covered by its contracts. Experimental/live-only Runnable only under the page's explicit live capabilities; never captured or run in CI. Design—not shipped A proposal outside the current implementation boundary.

docs.title: M10 local-author design
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

This page is the subordinate design record for #151 (M10.0). The milestone roadmap owns status, order, gates, and exclusions. The implementation plan owns technical staging. Journey 2's Experiment declaration and dual-form run() call are shipped by M10.1, Journey 1's improve() call is shipped by M10.2, Journey 3's functional search is shipped by M10.3, and the aggregate Run.inspect() read model is shipped by M10.4. Journey 4's Session is shipped by M10.6. The read-only local browser shipped in M10.7; frozen-payload artifact presentation, previews, diffs, and canonical attachments shipped in M10.8. At the time of this record the parent M10 remained open. Its current status is owned by the milestone roadmap.

The live examples were later reorganized by user journey under examples/learn/, domains/, operations/, agents/, and research/. Numbered paths below are frozen historical measurement evidence; the live functional-search fixtures now reside at examples/learn/functional_search/, and the live future reservation is examples/research/trusted_workers/.

The public story is: proposers create candidates, evaluators judge them, search decides what to try next, and Meta-Evolve records the entire process.

docs.title: Vocabulary tiers
docs.text:
The beginner tier names the seed, proposer, evaluator, and bounded trials=. The declarative tier adds Task, Experiment, search, context, experience, random seed, and registry. Storage, execution mode, and a narrowing budget are execution overlays. The extension tier retains SearchProgram.next() and the kernel records needed by advanced policy authors.

trials= is an author-facing cost and control limit, not exposure of kernel Trial records. Search state, trial specifications, operators, work items, events, and raw randomness stay off the simple path.

docs.title: Measurement rules
docs.text:
A physical line is every nonblank, non-comment code line. Imports and lines containing only delimiters count. Every counted line is classified once: algorithm expresses the limit, selection, stopping, or domain declaration; scaffolding adapts protocols, identities, execution, or syntax around those choices. Proposer, evaluator, and artifact-domain logic is held outside every search slice.

The shipped before-side for functional search is this runnable full-protocol shape, reduced from the repository's custom-search test without changing its protocol work:

from meta_evolve import domain
class IncumbentRefinement:
    policy = domain.PolicyRef("example:incumbent", "1", origin="local")
    def __init__(self, proposer):
        self.proposer = domain.ComponentRef.local_proposer(proposer)
    def next(self, state):
        if state.usage.trials >= 20:
            return domain.Stop(reason="trial limit reached")
        parent = state.incumbent_id or state.start.seed_artifact_id
        return domain.TrialSpec(
            task_id=state.start.task_id,
            parent_ids=(parent,),
            proposer=self.proposer,
            operator=domain.OperatorSpec(kind="rewrite"),
            budget=domain.Budget(trials=1, evaluations=1),
            random_seed=state.randomness.seed("trial"),
        )
search = IncumbentRefinement(propose)

It has 18 total lines: 3 algorithm and 15 scaffolding. It has one kernel import and constructs a trial manually. Changing only the name and limit for the two composition fixtures leaves those counts unchanged.

docs.title: Journey 1: beginner improve()
docs.text:
The smallest shipped declaration is bounded and can choose durable storage without claiming durable-local reconstruction:

run = meta.improve(
    seed=(),
    proposer=complete_one,
    evaluator=len,
    trials=3,
    storage=storage,
)

docs.title: Journey 2: explicit expansion
docs.text:
The shipped beginner call lowers exactly to this declaration and execution:

experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=meta.Task(evaluator=len),
    seed=(),
    proposer=complete_one,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=3),
)
run = meta.run(experiment, storage=storage)

docs.title: Journey 3: functional incumbent refinement
docs.text:
The shipped author-owned equivalent of the full-protocol before-side is:

@meta.search(max_trials=20)
def incumbent_refinement(search):
    return search.expand(search.incumbent or search.seed)

The callback sees opaque occurrence-preserving seed and incumbent handles, immutable declared configuration, expand(), and stop(). The adapter owns budgets, proposer and operator binding, replayed stopping, and named randomness.

docs.title: Journey 4: uninterrupted, paced, and resumed Session
docs.text:
Uninterrupted execution remains one call:

run = meta.run(experiment, storage=storage)

Paced execution completes one committed decision per step:

with meta.Session.start(
    experiment,
    storage=storage,
    budget=budget,
    mode="local",
) as session:
    for decision in session:
        observe(decision)
run = session.run

Recovery continues the same authority and budget rather than accepting a new decision:

with meta.Session.resume(
    run_id,
    storage=storage,
    registry=registry,
) as session:
    for decision in session:
        observe(decision)
run = session.run

Uninterrupted and resumed execution must produce byte-identical durable histories. Human choices require a future declared component with recorded inputs; Session.step(decision=...) is prohibited.

docs.title: Journey 5: deterministic textual-feedback descent
docs.text:
This shipped functional-search fixture is derived from the deterministic development loop in examples/20_harness_evolution/; its proposer, evaluator, artifact domain, and held-out promotion check remain outside the slice:

@meta.search(max_trials=2)
def textual_feedback_descent(search):
    """Expand the incumbent after deterministic development feedback."""
    return search.expand(search.incumbent or search.seed)

It is a deterministic, local, unpaid, unnumbered fixture under examples/functional_search/, not a new numbered example.

docs.title: Journey 6: deterministic AutoResearch composition
docs.text:
This shipped outer-search fixture is derived from examples/19_autoresearch/; private selection, public evidence, inner runs, and held-out evaluation remain evaluator- or user-owned:

@meta.search(max_trials=2)
def autoresearch_recipe(search):
    """Expand the selected recipe for the next bounded outer evaluation."""
    return search.expand(search.incumbent or search.seed)

It is also deterministic, local, unpaid, unnumbered under examples/functional_search/, and outside the numbered sequence. Neither fixture creates or consumes the reserved examples/22_trusted_workers/.

docs.title: Friction scorecard
docs.text:
This is the historical M10.0 measurement, so its original proposed slice labels and line counts remain unchanged as later journeys ship.

Public names count distinct public API names in the slice; kernel imports count import statements from internal extension namespaces. A durability rewrite is an author change required to move from local execution to durable-local reconstruction. Reduction is the drop in scaffolding from the 15-line shipped functional-search baseline; it is published only where that comparison applies. The now-runnable Journey 5 and Journey 6 fixtures are statically recounted by the same rules at 3 algorithm lines and 1 scaffolding line each. Both therefore retain the published 93% reduction, well above the required 50%; the historical scorecard labels and measurements below remain unchanged.

Journey Slice Public names User-visible concepts Total Algorithm Scaffolding Kernel imports Manual trials First failure Durability rewrites Reduction 1 Beginner proposed 1 seed, proposer, evaluator, trials, storage, run 7 4 3 0 No invalid declarations fail before work; proposal and evaluation failures are typed outcomes graduate to Experiment and register components — 2 Expansion proposed 4 task, experiment, search, execution overlay 7 4 3 0 No duplicate or invalid declarations fail before work register reconstructible components and select durable-local mode — 3 Full protocol before 6 policy identity, state, trial, operator, budget, randomness 18 3 15 1 Yes malformed decisions fail at the protocol boundary provide a registered policy factory — 3 Functional proposed 1 limit, incumbent, seed, expand 3 2 1 0 No unsupported returns name expand() and stop() register the decorated policy for reconstruction 93% 4 Three execution forms proposed 2 experiment, overlays, decision, session, recovery 18 2 16 0 No start/resume validation fails before external work; later failures remain typed resume adds run id, storage, and registry, not new authority — 5 Textual feedback before 6 full policy and trial protocol 18 3 15 1 Yes malformed decisions fail at the protocol boundary provide a registered policy factory — 5 Textual feedback proposed 1 limit, incumbent, feedback-paced expansion 4 3 1 0 No unsupported returns fail with façade guidance register the decorated policy for reconstruction 93% 6 AutoResearch before 6 full policy and trial protocol 18 3 15 1 Yes malformed decisions fail at the protocol boundary provide a registered policy factory — 6 AutoResearch proposed 1 outer limit, selected recipe, expansion 4 3 1 0 No unsupported returns fail with façade guidance register the decorated policy for reconstruction 93%

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• SearchProgram.next() remains the full 1.x extension protocol. Renaming it to decide() adds churn while @meta.search removes routine exposure.
  • Decorator configuration is immutable, serializable, and identity-visible. Hidden closure configuration is rejected. Lowering is exact and introduces no coordinator branch or special case.
  • Outer and inner loops, generations, and episodes remain relative explanatory terms, not new core types.
  • Dictionary-returning CLI factories remain supported through 1.x and now emit the M10.1 DeprecationWarning beside the typed alternative; removal is no earlier than 2.0.
  • M10.3 #164 shipped the docstring-derived DecisionDescription contract.

docs.title: Deferred and rejected alternatives
docs.text:
After M10, class-based harness surfaces may remove repeated field names and named search/context presets may improve discovery only when they lower exactly through existing validation, identity, authority, and durability contracts. Reflective proposer recipes remain user-owned.

Rejected alternatives are ambient configuration, execution-owning forward(), optimizer-owned compile(), hidden captured configuration, injected human decisions, fused proposer/evaluator/search layers, and any sugar that requires a coordinator, kernel, artifact, provider, or infrastructure special case.

docs.title: M8 harness-evolution design brief
docs.text:
