Status: Design—not shipped. This retained decision brief records the design that preceded M8 implementation. Current executable semantics live in the shipped programming model and architecture. The canonical milestone records M8 as shipped; this historical brief cannot reopen its closure gate.

Design one bounded experiment: start from a worker harness containing a planner prompt and context policy; let an outer proposer change only those surfaces; score each candidate on fresh held-out repository tasks under equal budgets; compare it with the unchanged harness; leave promotion external.

The deterministic demonstration is examples/research/harness_evolution/.

Its execution boundary is decision-complete: the example accepts a user-owned proposer callable, CI drives it with a deterministic fixture-backed SDK client, and an opt-in maintainer driver may invoke a real SDK through the same callable shape. See the user-owned SDK boundary. The first authorized live run is captured once and sanitized without dropping regressions, ties, or failures. Evaluation, equal budgets, mutation authority, and promotion remain outside the wrapper.

docs.title: Map onto current seams
docs.text: M8 concept Current seam HarnessArtifact Artifact codecs, registries, component identity, and lineage MutationSurface Proposal validation, policy violations, and workspace capture Held-out evaluation Evaluators launching bounded fresh inner runs Harness comparison Run summaries, usage, failures, and comparison validity External promotion A governance decision after search selection SDK execution A user-owned callable returning a candidate or ProposalResult

docs.title: Locked executable decisions
docs.text:
• Search evaluates development episodes. Held-out episodes evaluate only the unchanged baseline and selected candidate, each with Greedy(max_trials=0).
  • Candidate encoding is followed by generic core-side successor validation before artifact commit. MutationSurface.apply() is convenience only.
  • The parent declares mutable surfaces. Successors cannot change parameter names/types, component references, interfaces, or non-surface state.
  • Planner text and context policy are independent implementations governed by one published conformance suite.
  • Evaluator identity includes exact suite content, worker/model declaration, budgets, timeouts, environment, and scoring/aggregation rule.
  • Resume guarantees begin at a committed outer evaluation. Uncommitted inner work may repeat.
  • One held-out fixture demonstrates the boundary; it is not statistically strong promotion evidence.

docs.title: Implemented artifact and identity
docs.text: The built-in artifact is agent-harness / harness-manifest-v1, with exactly one TextParam planner and one PolicyParam context policy. Existing artifact occurrence identity, content digest, lineage, and component references apply.

docs.title: Mutation authority
docs.text: Only text and policy configuration change. The codec returns InvalidOutput for malformed/no-op transitions and PolicyViolation for authority expansion; the proposal, evidence, and typed failure commit without a successor artifact.

docs.title: Held-out evaluation
docs.text: Portable episode values and fresh inner runs are implemented. Hidden tests and process controls remain evaluator-only; captured attempts, diagnostics, diffs, failures, and counts become outer evidence.

docs.title: Comparison and promotion
docs.text: compare_harnesses enforces the full equality gate and reports quality, actual usage, failures, verdict, and eligibility. best() never deploys anything.

docs.title: Replay and extensions
docs.text: Outer episode capture is ordinary durable evidence. Fault injection proves a committed outer evaluation is not repeated. Both built-in surfaces pass the same published suite without a coordinator branch.

docs.title: Historical live evidence
docs.text: The first authorized official-SDK result is committed without dropping its failures or tie: strict output-schema validation rejected both proposal calls, so no native mutation reached decoding or successor validation. Later authorized runs reached that boundary in closed, unmerged PR #162. The milestone record owns the closure and carefully limits what that retained evidence supports.

docs.title: Acceptance evidence
docs.text:
• Valid prompt and context-policy mutations use one ordinary coordinator path.
  • Authority violations are typed rejections with no successor artifact.
  • Composite identity, lineage, component provenance, nested usage, and failures replay.
  • Held-out inner runs are fresh and comparison fails closed on mismatched controls.
  • Resume performs no committed episode twice.
  • Promotion remains an explicit external outcome.

Final review must make candidate authority, distinct causal identity, parent lineage (the parent lineage invariant), effective budget, every typed failure, replay, comparison validity, and promotion ownership explicit.

docs.title: Meta-evolution
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

M9's deliberately small trusted policy-artifact slice is shipped and owned by the policy-evolution guide and canonical architecture. This page now records only future generalization beyond that slice; it defines no additional shipped classes.

docs.title: Inner and outer loops
docs.text:
Future outer candidates may describe broader harnesses or policies. Their evaluators would run fresh, bounded inner meta.run() episodes against an experiment-controlled suite. Inner artifacts, trials, evaluations, failures, evidence, and usage would retain their own identities while linking to the outer evaluation.

The candidate could change only a declared mutation surface. It could not change the suite, hidden splits, evaluator, enclosing budget, permissions, cache semantics, or promotion rule.

docs.title: Broader policy meta-evolution
docs.text: M9 already compares its two-field policy artifacts under exact controls. Any broader policy space must remain compatible across task distribution, model, evaluator, environment, seeds, and budgets. Aggregation must preserve uncertainty and typed failures rather than average missing measurements into low scores. Held-out results remain unavailable until the relevant evaluation permits them.

docs.title: Nested budgets
docs.text:
Outer and inner evaluation, trial, token, and wall limits require explicit reservation and settlement. Inner exhaustion cannot consume undeclared outer authority. Cache reuse is valid only when every behavior-affecting declaration matches.

M8 and M9 used decision-complete designs and the harness_evolution and policy_evolution examples. See the M8 design and milestone roadmap.

docs.title: Distributed and network direction
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

The shipped execution profiles are local and durable-local. Distribution begins only after local semantics remain stable under concurrency and failure.

docs.title: Trusted distribution
docs.text: A trusted worker design needs durable attempts, leases, renewal, expiry, cancellation, idempotent result submission, capability matching, and atomic budget reservation/settlement. Delivery retries retain one logical trial. Out-of-order wall-clock completion cannot change logical random choices or reveal future experience.

docs.title: Federation
docs.text:
Cross-institution exchange additionally needs scoped identities, signed manifests, visibility, licensing, attribution, embargo, retraction, disputes, and task-specific trust. Policy-filtered subgraphs may preserve causal shape while redacting content.

Worker liveness, service health, queue estimates, and caches are ephemeral. Accepted artifacts, evaluations, budgets, authority changes, and promotion decisions remain durable. No network design may weaken candidate authority or failure honesty.

docs.title: Scientific direction
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Meta-Evolve may eventually represent hypotheses, protocols, datasets, simulations, analyses, claims, replications, and retractions as typed artifacts. That direction does not make software evaluation equivalent to validated science.

Scientific use requires explicit provenance, preregistered or otherwise governed evaluation, uncertainty, leakage controls, independent replication, negative results, and human/institutional authority. Model-generated novelty or an improved benchmark score is evidence only within the declared experiment.

Training views, semantic retrieval, learned search, and model-weight updates must be derived from immutable authorized records. They cannot become an unrecorded source of experience or retroactively alter a historical decision.

Current shipped semantics provide useful ingredients—immutable artifacts, typed failures, evidence, budgets, causal lineage, and replay—but do not ship a scientific artifact domain or make generalization claims.

docs.title: Future search policies
docs.text:
Status: Design—not shipped.

Meta-Evolve currently ships deterministic Greedy, BestOfN, BestOfK, Population, Specialists, and TreeSearch presets. The ideas below are roadmap direction, not importable names or accepted semantics.

docs.title: Pareto and quality-diversity archives
docs.text: Multi-objective archives would need explicit dominance, constraint, tie, capacity, and admission decisions. Quality-diversity additionally needs a versioned behavior descriptor and deterministic binning. Archive membership must be replayable from recorded evaluations rather than recomputed under a new definition.

docs.title: Islands and migration
docs.text: An island design must distinguish artifact identity from island membership. Migration is a recorded search decision, not artifact copying or Git history. Timing, topology, migrant selection, admission, and random streams must remain deterministic at the logical level.

docs.title: Other bandits and tree allocation
docs.text:
TreeSearch ships fixed progressive widening, best-descendant backup, and deterministic UCT descent; it does not imply the broader allocation ideas below are importable names or accepted semantics. Any other allocation policy may use uncertainty, cost, or upper-confidence estimates only when their observations, update rule, and random choices are explicit. Retry delivery must never become an extra logical trial.

No future policy may erase failed outcomes, widen budgets, inspect hidden evaluation, or require a coordinator special case.

docs.title: User-owned SDK boundary
docs.text: Status: Design—not shipped. This retained decision record preceded the deterministic M8 flagship and opt-in driver; the authorized live capture is still pending. The callable boundary itself and the hard-removal migration it gates are shipped; the migration guide is their canonical record. This page adds no agent runtime, provider adapter, or M8 domain type.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Meta-Evolve accepts an ordinary callable or an object with a structural propose() method. The user invokes and configures any model SDK inside that boundary. The SDK owns authentication, sessions, tools, permissions, structured decoding, and provider telemetry. Meta-Evolve owns candidate validation, independent evaluation, budgets, durable records, lineage, experience auditing, and promotion authority.

There is no provider ABC and no generic agent runtime. A direct candidate return remains the smallest path; ProposalResult is the typed path when a wrapper has usage, evidence, metadata, or derivation to report.

SDK wrapper output Meta-Evolve destination Decoded artifact value ProposalResult.candidate Total tokens and elapsed time Usage.tokens and Usage.wall_seconds Charged monetary cost Usage.spend_micros Raw response, estimated cost, model, granular tokens, provider telemetry EvidenceDraft or metadata Audited observations actually used derived_from

Trial and evaluation counts are coordinator-owned. A wrapper that reports either count is normalized to typed InvalidOutput, and completion overwrites both counts independently as defense in depth. Granular token categories remain provider evidence. Charged monetary cost was promoted to the shared Usage.spend_micros field by issue #143; estimates still remain evidence with their price basis.

Ordinary SDK exceptions become ProposerFailure. Framework failures that state a fact about durable state, accounting, or run capability escape unchanged: EventStreamConflict, DurableCorruption, InvalidSearchHistory, ExperienceStoreUnavailable, ExecutionAccountingUnknown, and CapabilityError.

docs.title: Audited agent pull
docs.text:
A user wrapper may register an SDK custom tool whose handler delegates to the scoped context.experience reader. The handler returns only the authorized observation and retains the observation references that the SDK actually used; the wrapper returns those references in ProposalResult.derived_from.

SDK tool call
  -> user handler
  -> context.experience.search/open/ancestors/siblings/compare
  -> audited, bounded observation
  -> SDK
  -> ProposalResult(derived_from=used_references)

The callback can be in-process or forwarded through a user-owned RPC bridge. Meta-Evolve adds no process or tool protocol for that bridge. Access denial, exhaustion, audit-store failure, and unknown accounting keep their existing semantics because the handler delegates to the scoped reader rather than copying or bypassing it. SDKs without custom-tool support may receive pushed context.bundle content, but that is not agent-directed pull.

docs.title: M8 flagship execution
docs.text:
The examples/research/harness_evolution/ demonstration accepts a user-owned proposer callable. CI uses a deterministic fixture-backed SDK client. The opt-in maintainer driver invokes a real SDK through the same callable boundary, without a package dependency or a shipped provider example.

The first authorized live M8 run must be captured once, sanitized, and retained honestly. The capture must preserve ties, regressions, typed failures, and unsuccessful attempts rather than rewriting them into a success narrative. It must identify the wrapper declaration and the controls that affect behavior.

The wrapper may propose only manifest-declared planner and context-policy changes. External evaluators run fresh held-out episodes under equal effective budgets. Candidate code cannot change evaluation, grants, hidden inputs, budgets, promotion rules, or mutation authority. best() selects a recorded result; promotion remains a separate governed action.

The provider removal was gated on this boundary and the audited experience bridge being complete, and shipped in the same change as both. No The M8 types are implemented elsewhere; this decision still adds no provider ABC, agent runtime, or core SDK adapter.

docs.title: Removal and evidence policy
docs.text:
The pre-1.0 migration is a hard removal: first-party Claude and Codex imports, extras, adapters, fixtures, and live tests receive no compatibility shim. Historical experiments and milestone records remain accessible and are labeled superseded. Their original claims are evidence of what was tested at the time; they are not current package instructions or shipped fixtures.

The repository boundary applies to current src/, examples, and shipped guides. Provider names remain legitimate in historical experiments, milestone records, design decisions, and migration material.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
You will improve one customer-support response. The ticket reports a duplicate $49 charge for order #4021. The seed is polite but gives no concrete refund action; the proposer adds an action and timeline without claiming the refund already happened.

The evaluator is deliberately mechanical. It checks only the order id, a concrete $49 refund action, and the absence of a false completion claim.

Before you run it, here is the whole lifecycle: Meta-Evolve evaluates the seed as a baseline, asks the proposer for one successor, evaluates that successor with the same grader, and selects the higher-scoring measured response. The proposer never sees or changes the evaluator.

docs.title: Complete program
docs.text:
import meta_evolve as meta


SEED = "I'm sorry about the duplicate $49 charge for order #4021. I'm looking into it."


def propose(_parent):
    return "I'm sorry about the duplicate $49 charge for order #4021. I'll submit a $49 refund today; it should appear in 5–7 business days."


def grade(reply):
    checks = ("#4021" in reply, "$49" in reply and "refund" in reply.lower(), "already refunded" not in reply.lower() and "refund is complete" not in reply.lower())
    return sum(checks) / len(checks)


result = meta.improve(seed=SEED, proposer=propose, evaluator=grade, trials=1)
print(result.best())

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
Execution is optional while reading. From a repository checkout, run:

uv run python examples/learn/support_response/quickstart.py
Output
I'm sorry about the duplicate $49 charge for order #4021. I'll submit a $49 refund today; it should appear in 5–7 business days.

docs.title: Read the declaration
docs.text:
improve() receives four job-level inputs:

Input Role in this run seed The initial response and evaluated baseline proposer A callable that creates a possible successor evaluator An independent callable that assigns the three-check score trials The maximum number of proposed successors, excluding the seed

The seed passes two checks: it contains #4021 and makes no false completion claim, but it promises no refund action. Its score is 2/3. The successor passes all three checks, so best() prints it with score 1.0. The output is the selected artifact value, not a deployment or a message sent to a customer.

docs.title: Distinguish poor work from failure
docs.text: A low score is rankable work. A proposer exception, malformed candidate, or grader exception is recorded as a typed, unrankable failure. Those distinctions matter once the grader is external or expensive: zero says “valid work measured poorly,” while a typed failure says no trustworthy score was produced.

docs.title: Change one thing and predict
docs.text:
Set trials=0. The proposer will not run, but the seed will still be evaluated as the baseline and returned by best(). Restore trials=1 before continuing so the next page has both the seed and its successor to inspect.

This page contains one experiment. Next, learn what its run returns.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text: You will install Meta-Evolve, verify the import, and know which execution mode you are using. The default path is local, in-memory, and dependency-free.

docs.title: Choose one installation path
docs.text:
For an application that already uses uv, add the released package to that application and verify that Python can import it:

uv add meta-evolve
uv run python -c "import meta_evolve; print(meta_evolve.__version__)"

The second command should print a version and exit successfully. uv add changes the application's dependency declaration; it does not create or run an evolution.

For a Meta-Evolve source checkout, reproduce the repository's locked development environment instead:

uv sync --locked --dev
uv run pytest -q

The test count may change as the project grows, but the command should finish without failures. You do not need the optional browser or a model-provider SDK for the first evolution.

docs.title: What gets installed
docs.text:
No model provider is required. A proposer and evaluator can be ordinary Python callables. Durable storage, a user-owned SDK, and subprocess grading are opt-in edges introduced later.

The default improve() call runs synchronously in the current Python process and stores its history in memory. Closing the process discards that in-memory history; persistence is a separate choice covered later.

docs.title: Installation failures are not evaluation results
docs.text:
If import fails, fix the environment before starting an experiment; an import or installation error is not a poor candidate score. If a later run records a typed failure, inspect the returned run instead of treating it as zero.

Next, run your first evolution.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
You will query a successful run for its winner and history, then diagnose a run where nothing was rankable. A Run is a read-only handle over committed facts; the queries do not rerun the proposer or evaluator.

The support example below performs one experiment declaration twice for a fair comparison, then creates an isolated failure variant solely to show diagnosis. The successful run and the failure-only run are separate histories; creating the diagnostic example cannot contaminate the successful result.

docs.title: Complete results tour
docs.text:
"""Tour every public result-query job with the support-response run."""

from __future__ import annotations

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve.domain import EvaluatorFailure
from meta_evolve.errors import RunsNotComparable

from rubric import SEED, grade_response, propose_response, support_task, run_support


def all_failures() -> meta.Run:
    def broken_grader(_candidate):
        return EvaluatorFailure(message="judge service unavailable")

    return meta.improve(
        seed=SEED,
        proposer=lambda parent: parent,
        evaluator=broken_grader,
        trials=1,
    )


def incompatible_run() -> meta.Run:
    def changed_grader(candidate):
        return grade_response(candidate)

    task = support_task()
    changed_task = meta.Task(
        evaluator=changed_grader,
        objectives=task.objectives,
        budget=task.budget,
    )
    return meta.run(
        meta.Experiment(
            task=changed_task,
            seed=SEED,
            proposer=propose_response,
            search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=2),
        )
    )


def main() -> None:
    result = run_support(random_seed=0)
    second = run_support(random_seed=1)
    winner = result.best()
    trial = result.best_trial()
    print(f"best={winner.value}")
    print(f"best_trial={trial.logical_step}:{trial.metrics['overall']:.2f}")
    print(f"lineage={[item.logical_step for item in result.lineage(winner)]}")
    print(f"trials={[item.state for item in result.trials()]}")
    print(f"summary={result.summary().primary_score:.2f}")
    overview = result.inspect().overview
    print(f"inspect={overview.lifecycle}/{overview.rankability}")
    print(f"compare_tied={result.compare(second).tied}")
    try:
        result.compare(incompatible_run())
    except RunsNotComparable:
        print("compare_refusal=changed evaluator")

    failed = all_failures()
    try:
        failed.best()
    except meta.NoSuccessfulEvaluation:
        failures = [type(item.failure).__name__ for item in failed.inspect().trials]
        print(f"all_failure_diagnosis={failures}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
uv run python examples/learn/support_response/results.py
Output
best=I understand the duplicate $49 charge on order #4021 is frustrating. I'll request a $49 refund within one business day.
best_trial=1:1.00
lineage=[0, 1]
trials=['evaluated', 'evaluated', 'evaluated']
summary=1.00
inspect=complete/rankable
compare_tied=True
compare_refusal=changed evaluator
all_failure_diagnosis=['EvaluatorFailure', 'EvaluatorFailure']

docs.title: Choose the query for the question
docs.text:
All seven queries read already committed facts. None reruns the proposer or evaluator.

Query Question it answers Requires a rankable result? best() Which artifact won on the primary objective? Yes best_trial() What metrics and evidence belong to that winner? Yes lineage() Which causal path produced an artifact? Only when no target is supplied trials() What happened on every seed evaluation and proposal attempt? No summary() What portable score, usage, and identity summary describes the run? Yes inspect() What was declared, attempted, spent, and failed? No compare() How do two compatible run summaries differ? Yes, on both sides

The output shows the winner at logical step 1, whose lineage is the seed at step 0 followed by that successor. Three evaluated states mean the seed and two proposal trials all produced measurements. complete/rankable says the run stopped normally and has at least one usable metric.

An objective name passed to best("timeline") or best_trial("timeline") queries that declared metric instead of the primary overall metric. It does not change how the run originally ranked candidates.

docs.title: Diagnose a run without a winner
docs.text: best(), best_trial(), lineage() without a target, and summary() raise NoSuccessfulEvaluation when no evaluation has metrics. trials() and inspect() still work and preserve each typed failure. That is why the example catches NoSuccessfulEvaluation and then prints two EvaluatorFailure records: the evaluator failed for both the seed and the attempted successor.

docs.title: Change one query and predict
docs.text:
Print result.best_trial("timeline").metrics["timeline"] in main(). The value is 1.0: the query selects on the declared timeline metric, while the stored trials and the original primary-objective winner remain unchanged.

Next, grade with checks and rubrics.

docs.title: Custom search
docs.text:
Use @meta.search when a policy needs only seed/incumbent selection, expansion, and an explicit stop. The component playground is the canonical executable example.

Implement the full SearchProgram.next(state) protocol only when a current job needs decisions the facade cannot express. A custom program returns typed trial, archive, or stop decisions; it does not invoke proposers, evaluate candidates, mutate projections, or allocate beyond state.remaining_budget.

Keep configuration canonical and identity-visible, use recorded named random substreams, and pass the policy conformance suite. The coordinator must remain unchanged when the custom policy is installed.

docs.title: Project status
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. Meta-Evolve ships the local evaluated-evolution system through M10, including callable and expanded experiments, typed artifacts, replaceable search and context, audited experience, durable local execution, source evaluation, inspection, comparison, sessions, CLI, and the optional read-only browser.

M8's deterministic harness implementation and retained closure evidence are shipped. M8.7's bounded source listing, reads, diffs, and disposable Git presentation are shipped. M9 and M9.5 ship policy artifacts plus BestOfK, Specialists, and TreeSearch. Monetary P1 ships exact spend_micros accounting and post-hoc enforcement.

Production provider calls and infrastructure remain user-owned. The production-agent composition is Experimental/live-only because this repository retains no production-scale run. M11 trusted distribution, M12 federation, monetary reservation/settlement, and the post-M10 notebook-presentation follow-up remain Design—not shipped.

The milestones are authoritative for scope and status. The programming model owns public execution contracts, the architecture owns stable semantics, and implementation plan records technical staging.

docs.title: Local run browser
docs.text: Status: Shipped. M10.7–M10.8 provide an optional, read-only presentation over shipped Storage, inspection, artifact presentation, diff, comparison, and exact-version contracts.

docs.title: Start it
docs.text:
Install the optional dependencies, then point the command at an existing durable store:

uv sync --extra browser
meta-evolve ui --storage ./store --port 8000

Runs using a custom artifact codec can reconstruct it through the ordinary experiment-module convention:

meta-evolve ui --storage ./store --module experiments.my_run

The optional module is loaded only after browser dependencies are available. Only its experiment().registry enters the browser reader; proposers, evaluators, policies, sessions, and execution are never invoked. Without the module or codec, the run is an ordinary actionable codec-unavailable 422 state rather than corruption.

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. The host is fixed to loopback and the server uses one worker. The browser has no write, run, resume, cancellation, promotion, or deletion controls. It has no authentication. Loopback binding limits its intended scope; it is not a claim that the application is safe to proxy or publish remotely.

The pages are complete server-rendered HTML. Search, detail, comparison, lineage tables, and navigation work with JavaScript disabled. A small same-origin script only polls committed stream versions and reloads after facts change. A complete run page with a stable version carries no polling attributes at all; only the catalog and incomplete or unstable pages poll.

docs.title: What appears
docs.text:
The catalog is ordered lexicographically by content-derived run ID; it makes no chronological claim. Cards show task identity, lifecycle, rankability, policy, the primary objective and available score, artifact kind, and usage. Search filters those recorded fields.

A detail page follows the recorded story: overview, declaration, lineage, trials, evidence and failures, recorded artifact history, and decision timeline. The SVG lineage diagram has a semantic table containing the same parent edges. The history table preserves recorded occurrence order without calling it time, keeps occurrence identity separate from content digest, and offers one explicit diff choice for every parent.

Artifact pages show identity, parents, bounded specialized presentation, exact canonical attachment, and every available parent diff. Text, source trees, skill sets, canonical Python values, harnesses, and policy artifacts have fixed views. A custom kind receives deterministic canonical-payload text and an explicit no-specialized-view notice. All content originates in the frozen payload; decoded ArtifactView.value is never read, stringified, or passed to templates. Evidence URIs remain inert text, never links.

Direct-parent diffs support Text, SourceTree, and SkillSet. They identify added, removed, modified, and unchanged files and label added, removed, and unchanged lines textually as well as visually. A file whose content is identical on both sides reports its unchanged status without lines and consumes none of the shared diff budgets. Foreign-run views, non-parent edges, and incompatible families are refused with 422. Multi-parent occurrences never acquire an arbitrary default parent.

Bounds apply in this order: lexicographic path sorting; first 100 entries; 64 KiB UTF-8 per retained preview document; 256 KiB aggregate preview input; 64 KiB per diff side and 256 KiB aggregate diff input before invoking the diff algorithm; then 4,000 output lines. Final partial and omitted states remain visible. Canonical downloads are not truncated.

Comparison always receives an explicit ordered pair and invokes the public Run.compare() contract. It reports score, usage, winner or tie, and the three declaration flags. Incompatible or unrankable pairs remain visible as typed refusals; the browser does not pre-filter candidates or turn failure into a score.

docs.title: Replay and caches
docs.text:
One dedicated thread creates Storage.read_only(), performs every listing, version query, inspection, and comparison, and closes the handle. Route handlers and Starlette's general threadpool never receive it. This preserves SQLite connection affinity while concurrent HTTP requests queue safely.

The first catalog request performs one validated replay for every discovered run. It keeps one lightweight card per run, stamped with the exact run_version it observed and replaced when a newer version appears, plus a 32-entry LRU of full inspections. Comparisons use a separate 32-entry LRU keyed by the ordered IDs and both exact versions. Eviction discards only derived views, never durable facts. Inspections retain each frozen payload beside the decoded object, without eagerly storing an additional serialized byte copy; payload-heavy runs therefore consume proportionally more memory inside the bounded LRU. A comparison cache miss pays the public API's full multi-replay cost.

Before replay, the reader polls exact versions. Exact hits avoid replay; completed cached runs are not polled again. Catalog polling still calls Storage.runs() to discover additions and checks versions of incomplete runs.

Inspection reads a version before and after replay. A mismatch is retried once. If commits continue, the valid inspection snapshot is served without a version label or cache entry. Comparison is stricter: both versions must remain stable across the complete public comparison. A second mismatch returns retryable 503 rather than presenting a mixed observation.

docs.title: Failures and safety
docs.text:
Unknown or concurrently missing runs and artifact occurrences return 404. Comparison and diff refusals and codec capability gaps return escaped 422 pages. Transient store failures and unstable comparisons return 503. Corruption and unexpected defects return a safe 500 without a traceback or durable detail. A corrupt or codec-unavailable run becomes an isolated catalog error card so healthy runs remain reachable.

Store-open and schema failures happen before the server binds and use the ordinary CLI domain-failure path. Responses include a restrictive content security policy, nosniff, no-referrer, and frame-denial headers. These defenses do not expand the browser beyond its local, unauthenticated scope.

Raw artifact responses use application/json, nosniff, and Content-Disposition: attachment with a digest-derived filename. The bytes are the current digest encoding, canonical-payload-v1, not a native artifact export and not an unconditional promise for every future durable format.

docs.title: Manual visual review checklist
docs.text:
For changes to browser templates or CSS, review the catalog, run, artifact, diff, refusal, truncation, and codec-unavailable fixtures with JavaScript disabled at both fixed viewports:

  • desktop: 1440 × 900;
  • mobile: 390 × 844.

Record completion in the PR. Check heading order, landmarks, skip link, visible keyboard focus, native controls, textual status labels, contained wide tables and preformatted text, single-column mobile layout, and reduced-motion mode. Screenshot automation remains out of scope for this milestone.

docs.title: Durability
docs.text:
Status: Shipped.

Storage composes artifact and event storage. In-memory storage is isolated to the process. Durable storage uses a verified filesystem artifact store plus an append-only SQLite event stream.

import meta_evolve as meta

storage = meta.Storage.durable(".meta-evolve/example")

docs.title: Store
docs.text: Pass durable storage to meta.run() to preserve committed artifacts, evidence, decisions, lineage, usage, and failures. mode="durable-local" additionally requires registered reconstructible components and their verified manifests. Validation happens before the first event is written.

docs.title: Reopen
docs.text:
Run reconstructs a read-only view from committed facts:

reopened = meta.Run(run_id, storage)
print(reopened.summary())

Reopen performs no proposal or evaluation. Local callable and SDK histories can be durable and inspectable even when their live components cannot be rebuilt.

For an inspection-only process, open the same directory without commit or execution authority:

with meta.Storage.read_only(".meta-evolve/example") as storage:
    version = storage.run_version(run_id)
    inspection = meta.Run(run_id, storage).inspect()

is_durable and is_read_only answer different questions. The first says committed facts live on durable media; the second says this handle cannot commit. Storage.durable(...) reports True, False, while Storage.read_only(...) reports True, True. Artifact, blob, event, and unit-of-work writes all raise CapabilityError. Passing the handle to run(), improve(), or resume() is rejected before a codec, registry component, proposer, evaluator, provider, or subprocess runs.

run_version(run_id) is the maximum committed event sequence. It returns 0 for a well-formed id with no events and uses a new deferred transaction on each call, so a long-lived reader observes successive atomic commits from a WAL writer. It is deliberately a cheap polling query, not a full integrity check. Run(run_id, storage).inspect() performs authoritative loading and still raises RunNotFound when that run is required but absent.

The optional local run browser owns one long-lived read-only handle on one dedicated thread. It calls runs() to discover additions, polls exact versions before replay, and never polls a cached completed run again. Its bounded caches are disposable observations; append-only storage and validated replay remain authoritative.

Read-only open requires an existing current store. It uses SQLite mode=ro plus query_only, and never creates a directory, changes journal settings, executes DDL, stamps a schema, or migrates. For an older or unstamped store, close readers and reopen it once with writable Storage.durable(...), then use Storage.read_only(...) again. Future schemas raise SchemaVersionRejected, malformed current schemas raise DurableCorruption, and missing or inaccessible database/filesystem/WAL state raises DurableStoreError with the underlying cause.

docs.title: Resume
docs.text:
resume verifies manifests, declarations, store integrity, and the recovery frontier before doing missing work. It retains the same run ID and never re-executes a committed operation. A non-resumable local history raises CapabilityError.

Use Session.resume to pace that same recovery:

with meta.Session.resume(run_id, storage=storage, registry=registry) as session:
    for decision in session:
        observe(decision)
result = session.run

Preparation validates and classifies the committed frontier but does not finish pending work. The first step() either completes the already committed trial or evaluation, or records and completes one new decision. Resuming an already stopped run iterates zero times; an explicit terminal step() returns the existing stop view without changing events or artifacts.

docs.title: Compare
docs.text: Reopened completed runs use the same comparison contract as live results. Declaration mismatches raise RunsNotComparable before ranking.

docs.title: Replay and reproducibility
docs.text:
Replay is a pure fold over immutable transitions and artifacts. It reconstructs logical decisions, projections, context selection, access audits, and usage without calling external systems. Named random streams reproduce deterministic local choices. Provider output is not promised to regenerate byte-for-byte; the durable guarantee is the exact committed transcript and declarations.

Corrupt bytes, unknown schemas, gaps, mismatched IDs, and incomplete atomic batches fail explicitly rather than falling back to a partial interpretation.

The searchable recovery chapter links the raw executed recovery notebook.

docs.title: Experience
docs.text: Status: Shipped. Experience is explicit and off by default.

docs.title: No memory
docs.text: With no context= or experience= declaration, a proposer receives no prior records. NoMemory states that policy explicitly when a named declaration is useful.

docs.title: Pushed context
docs.text:
A ContextPolicy selects a bounded bundle before each proposal. AncestorsOnly follows the current parent lineage; BestSibling exposes a bounded sibling view. The selected structured records, rendered text, reason, logical time, and usage are committed before the proposer runs.

import meta_evolve as meta

experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=task,
    seed=seed,
    proposer=proposer,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=3),
    context=meta.AncestorsOnly(max_records=4, max_chars=4000),
)
result = meta.run(experiment)

docs.title: Audited pull
docs.text:
PullAccess grants bounded operations, result counts, records, and characters. The proposer uses an ExperienceReader only inside that grant. Each request, result, denial, and usage charge is retained; hidden or future records fail closed through typed access errors.

For a SourceTree task, the same reader can inspect an exact prior artifact occurrence without receiving a whole repository implicitly:

artifacts = context.experience.search(record_kinds=("artifact",), limit=1)
artifact_ref = artifacts.references[0]

listing = context.experience.list_source_paths(artifact_ref, limit=20)
read = context.experience.read_source(
    artifact_ref,
    paths=("solver.py",),
)
return meta.ProposalResult(
    candidate=revise(parent, read.files[0].source),
    derived_from=(read.artifact_ref,),
)

Listings are lexicographic; reads preserve requested order. Both retain only a prefix of complete entries that fits the grant and charge the exact rendered characters. A missing path atomically denies the read. Canonical diff_source(older_ref, newer_ref) is also shipped: it verifies both prior occurrences, returns a bounded path-ordered unified diff, and charges two results. A source patch callback may instead request a bounded disposable Git presentation:

from meta_evolve.adapters import GitHistoryView

proposer = meta.PatchProposer(
    edit,
    history=GitHistoryView(
        max_ancestors=4,
        max_archive_members=2,
        max_chars=128_000,
    ),
)

The edit callback runs ordinary git log, git show, and git diff commands with cwd=context.workspace.root and env=context.workspace.environment. The selected parent remains HEAD; the manifest is available as context.workspace.history. Git metadata is external and disposable, and direct workspace mutation is rejected before the returned exact-file patch is applied. Whole-tree reader operations, semantic retrieval, and cross-run access are not shipped.

docs.title: Declared derivation
docs.text: A rich proposal may declare which authorized observations influenced it. Those references are validated against the experience it actually received. Empty derivation remains compatible with ordinary callables.

docs.title: Causal provenance
docs.text:
Everyday users can rely on Run.lineage(), Run.trials(), and RunExperienceUsage. Strict ledger ordering, logical-time validation, and replay are isolated in the advanced provenance reference. RunExperienceUsage.by_operation provides canonically ordered non-zero operation totals through meta_evolve.views.ExperienceOperationUsage; they sum exactly to the aggregate pull usage.

Experience changes what a proposer may observe, never the evaluator, budget, permission, or promotion authority.

docs.title: Evidence companions
docs.text: The searchable narrative wrappers cover the experience tour, push and pull, and derivation comparison. Each links its raw executed notebook: the tour, push/pull lab, and derivation lab.

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text: Status: Shipped. Add replaceable components at declared seams; never branch the coordinator on a concrete domain, provider, evaluator, policy, or backend.

docs.title: Artifact domains
docs.text:
An artifact codec declares a stable kind, representation, interfaces, canonical encode/decode behavior, and rejection boundary. Register it with Registry. The same codec encodes the seed and every successor; rejected values become typed invalid-output trials.

The complete artifact-domain tutorial is extracted, executed in a clean interpreter, and checked against the published codec conformance suite.

docs.title: Components and identity
docs.text: Local callables are convenient but not cold-resumable. Registered durable-local proposers, evaluators, search policies, and context policies use explicit component references plus behavior-affecting configuration. Resume rebuilds the recorded implementation from that registry and refuses mismatches.

docs.title: Published conformance
docs.text:
Every extension component family has a published reusable suite: codecs, repository-editing proposers, evaluators, search programs, context policies, workspaces, sandboxes, and typed mutation surfaces. Subclass one, name the subclass Test..., and override its fixtures and hooks. Each runs unchanged here against the built-in implementations (or, for the proposer suites, reference callables) plus at least one written the way an outside author would write it — MutationSurfaceTests against TextParam, PolicyParam, ParentSelection, and TrialLimit; SearchProgramTests against Greedy, BestOfN, BestOfK, Population, CandidatePolicy, and a next-only custom program.

The two proposer suites are exercised by in-repository reference callables (tests/test_proposer_conformance.py); no first-party provider adapter ships, so those callables are the reference subjects.

SandboxProviderTests checks the declared cwd and exact environment, verbatim argv, separated output streams, ordinary nonzero exits, enforced timeout, independent stdout/stderr byte ceilings, bounded partial output, and wall-only usage. Its timeout and probe-sleep fixtures are overridable for container and remote startup costs. Passing it does not prove filesystem isolation or that a provider executed rather than simulated every probe; CPU, memory, network, syscall, and broader execution isolation remain outside the suite.

ContextPolicy.select receives a typed, read-only ExperienceGraph. Import ExperienceGraph and ExperienceQuery from meta_evolve; the returned ExperienceNode, ExperienceRecord, and ExperienceState values are root exports too. Replay construction remains an application service, so helpers such as replay_experience_graph stay under meta_evolve.application.

State the limits rather than implying coverage that does not exist. A suite checks the laws it names and no others, and it makes an unexercised law visible: EvaluatorTests skips its typed-failure check when a subclass declares no rejected_candidates and its semantic oracle when it declares no scored_candidates, ArtifactCodecTests skips its aliasing law when mutable_values is () and its decode-validation law when rejected_payloads is (), and ContextPolicyTests makes a policy that selects nothing say so through expects_records. NoMemory is outside that suite, since meta.run normalizes it away before any policy runs.

The subclass contract follows one rule set, stated in the package docstring: required hooks raise NotImplementedError; optional laws skip visibly or cross-check a declaration; a law needing an uncontaminated second subject asks for a factory (make_evaluator, search_factory) and refuses the same object twice; laws observe subjects through kernel records or author-supplied projections, never the subject's own equality or self-report.

One trap is worth knowing when you write a codec: decode returning an equal value is not the same as returning an independent one. A codec that hands back the instance it was given lets an evaluator reach and edit the caller's own object. ArtifactCodecTests.mutable_values has no default for that reason — declaring () is a positive claim that your values are immutable, not a way to skip the question. Every value law observes through value_state, an observation the codec has no hand in — never through the value type's __eq__ (which usually ships with the codec and could certify a collapse) and never through the codec's own encode (which could special-case the watched objects); the default projection knows exact canonical and kernel types and refuses anything else. Mutable values additionally require mutate, the edit the aliasing law watches. rejected_payloads is the mirror of rejected_values on the decode side — decode is validation, and () is a positive claim that every payload decodes. EvaluatorTests.scored_candidates is the analogous semantic oracle: every other evaluator law holds for lambda c: 0.0, so state expected metrics wherever your scores are predictable. EvaluatorTests keeps a matching candidate-mutation law, so the failure is caught where it starts and where it does damage.

Store adapters keep an internal contract under tests/ and are not one of these families. The operations lab holds the coverage table.

docs.title: Migrating pre-1.0 conformance subclasses
docs.text:
The strengthened codec and mutation-surface laws intentionally changed their subclass fixtures. There are no compatibility aliases: update subclasses so the new laws run instead of silently retaining the weaker contract.

For codecs, rejected_payloads and mutable_values are now required. value_state must project custom values the default inert projection cannot read, and mutate is required only when mutable_values is non-empty.

Before:

class TestRecipeCodec(ArtifactCodecTests):
    @pytest.fixture
    def codec(self): return RecipeCodec()

    @pytest.fixture
    def values(self): return (Recipe(["mix"]),)

    @pytest.fixture
    def rejected_values(self): return (7,)

After:

class TestRecipeCodec(ArtifactCodecTests):
    # codec, values, and rejected_values stay as above
    @pytest.fixture
    def rejected_payloads(self): return (7, None)

    @pytest.fixture
    def mutable_values(self): return (Recipe(["mix"]),)

    def value_state(self, value): return tuple(value.steps)

    def mutate(self, value): value.steps.append("bake")

Return () from mutable_values for an immutable value type and omit mutate. Return () from rejected_payloads only when every canonical payload is valid input to decode; both empty tuples are positive claims.

For mutation surfaces, replace the singular mutation plus expected_surface fixtures with plural (mutation, expected_successor) pairs, and replace invalid_mutation with invalid_mutations.

Before:

@pytest.fixture
def mutation(self): return Rename("new")

@pytest.fixture
def expected_surface(self): return NameParam("new")

@pytest.fixture
def invalid_mutation(self): return Rename(7)

After:

@pytest.fixture
def mutations(self):
    return ((Rename("first"), NameParam("first")),
            (Rename("second"), NameParam("second")))

@pytest.fixture
def invalid_mutations(self):
    return (Rename(7),)

Keep surface, no_op_mutation, and foreign_mutation unchanged. Supply more than one valid pair wherever the domain allows, so an implementation that accepts one fixture value but substitutes its own value for others cannot pass.

docs.title: Design rule
docs.text:
Introduce a protocol only when a current acceptance test needs an independently testable second implementation. Keep the public call smaller than the internal port, preserve immutable inputs and typed failures, and make authority and accounting explicit.

The generated API reference lists every shipped root name and the namespaced harness and policy families. See the harness evolution and policy evolution guides.

docs.title: Harness evolution
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. The deterministic library and flagship are implemented. The separate official-SDK validation remains Experimental/live-only. Its first authorized capture is retained honestly as a schema-validation failure and tie; M8 closes only after a capture reaches native mutation decoding and core-side successor validation.

An agent harness is a typed composite artifact with two v1 mutation surfaces:

import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve import harness
from meta_evolve.domain import ComponentRef

baseline = harness.HarnessArtifact(
    planner=harness.TextParam(
        "planner",
        ComponentRef(role="planner", name="worker", version="1"),
        "planner-text/v1",
        "Inspect the task and make a conservative repair.",
    ),
    context_policy=harness.PolicyParam(
        "context_policy",
        ComponentRef(role="context-policy", name="context", version="1"),
        "context-policy/v1",
        {"diagnostics": False},
    ),
)

A user-owned TFD callable asks its SDK for native structured output matching HarnessMutation, uses baseline.apply(mutation) to construct the intended candidate, and returns an ordinary ProposalResult. The core independently compares every encoded successor with its parent before commit. Constructing a HarnessArtifact directly cannot bypass that check.

Search uses development episodes. Held-out evaluation is separate:

baseline_experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=held_out_task,
    seed=baseline,
    proposer=proposer,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=0),
)
candidate_experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=held_out_task,
    seed=selected.value,
    proposer=proposer,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=0),
)
baseline_result = meta.run(baseline_experiment)
candidate_result = meta.run(candidate_experiment)
comparison = meta.compare_harnesses(baseline_result, candidate_result)

if comparison.promotion_eligible:
    meta.export_harness(selected, destination)

compare_harnesses fails closed unless evaluator identity and its full configuration, artifact schema, objectives, effective budgets, proposer/search declarations, random seed, context, experience, and immutable harness declarations agree. The verdict is improvement, tie, regression, or unrankable. Eligibility never deploys or promotes anything.

RepositoryEpisode keeps its public seed separate from evaluator-only tests and bounded ProcessSpec. EpisodeSuite requires non-empty development and held-out splits with globally unique names, and both values expose stable content digests. Evaluator identity must cover the suite, worker/model, budgets, timeouts, environment, and scoring implementation.

Run the complete deterministic example:

uv run python examples/research/harness_evolution/main.py \
  --output /tmp/meta-evolve-m8

It records development quality 0.0 → 0.5 → 1.0, evaluates one untouched held-out repository only after selection, and exports the eligible selection. That single held-out fixture demonstrates the execution and authority boundary; it is not statistically strong promotion evidence.

docs.title: Migrate to a user-owned SDK wrapper
docs.text:
Status: Shipped. This is a deliberate pre-1.0 breaking change. There are no compatibility shims.

The following imports and extras were removed:

from meta_evolve.claude import Claude
from meta_evolve.codex import Codex
meta-evolve[claude]
meta-evolve[codex]

Install and authenticate your chosen SDK in your application, then call it from an ordinary proposer:

import meta_evolve as meta

def propose(parent, context):
    response = sdk.generate_structured(parent=parent)
    return meta.ProposalResult(
        candidate=response.candidate,
        usage=meta.Usage(
            tokens=response.input_tokens + response.output_tokens,
            spend_micros=response.charged_micros,
            wall_seconds=response.elapsed_seconds,
        ),
        metadata={"model": response.model},
        evidence=(
            meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="sdk-response", data=response.telemetry),
        ),
    )

experiment = meta.Experiment(task=task, seed=seed, proposer=propose)
result = meta.run(experiment)

The wrapper now owns authentication, sessions, tools, permissions, output decoding, retry behavior, and provider telemetry. Meta-Evolve continues to own candidate validation, external evaluation, budgets, durable records, lineage, experience auditing, and promotion authority.

For agent-directed pull, register an SDK custom tool whose handler delegates to context.experience, and return used observation references in ProposalResult.derived_from. SDKs without custom tools may receive pushed context.bundle data only.

The obsolete first-party adapter archive is no longer part of the source tree. Historical measurements remain recoverable from Git history and the closed M6 issues; they are not current fixtures or acceptance evidence.

See ProposalResult and ProposerContext for the promoted callable kit.

docs.title: Policy evolution
docs.text: Status: Shipped. Milestone 9 evaluates tiny declarative search-policy artifacts. Candidates never supply executable policy source.

docs.title: Declare the trusted artifact
docs.text:
from meta_evolve import policy

candidate = policy.PolicyArtifact(
    parent_selection=policy.ParentSelection("incumbent"),
    trial_limit=policy.TrialLimit(2),
)

The schema fixes both surface names, component declarations, interfaces, and allowed domains. PolicyMutation changes exactly one value. Wrapper-side apply() is convenient, while the built-in codec independently validates the encoded successor before artifact commit.

docs.title: Interpret it through an ordinary run
docs.text:
import meta_evolve as meta
from meta_evolve import policy

experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=episode.task,
    seed=episode.seed,
    proposer=episode.proposer,
    search=policy.CandidatePolicy(candidate),
    random_seed=episode.random_seed,
)
result = meta.run(experiment, budget=episode.budget)

seed parent selection behaves like independent best-of-N. incumbent behaves like greedy expansion. The artifact's trial limit is voluntary: the evaluator- owned inner budget remains authoritative. The canonical artifact payload is the registered candidate-policy@1 configuration, so durable reconstruction uses the existing policy registry and resume path.

docs.title: Capture episodes without adding a runtime
docs.text:
PolicyEpisode declares a task, canonically encoded seed, proposer, budget, random seed, and evaluator-owned environment. PolicySuite requires non-empty, unique development and held-out splits. Registered references are portable; local closures remain valid only for local composition.

User code executes ordinary meta.run() calls and records EpisodeOutcome values. Each outcome retains its inner RunId, evaluator-owned storage location, policy digest, quality, uncertainty, exact inner usage, typed failure or incomplete state, and exact-completed-run reuse flag. Development may reopen an exact completed run. Held-out execution uses a new empty namespace and never consults development results.

PolicyEvaluation recomputes aggregation from every outcome. A failed, incomplete, or missing episode makes the aggregate non-rankable without discarding partial evidence. Inner trials and evaluations stay inner usage; only actual tokens and elapsed time appear in outer_usage.

docs.title: Compare untouched held-out evidence
docs.text:
Evaluate the unchanged baseline and selected candidate in separate seed-only outer runs using Greedy(max_trials=0), then compare them:

comparison = meta.compare_policies(baseline_run, candidate_run)

Comparison fails closed on changed suites, splits, evaluator/aggregation identity, schemas, objectives, proposers, candidate-policy@1, effective budgets, environments, randomness, context, experience, or immutable surface declarations. Verdicts are improvement, tie, regression, or unrankable. compare_policies returns this report. promotion_eligible requires a strict, fully rankable improvement under equal controls. It reports evidence and never promotes or deploys.

Run the deterministic multi-episode flagship:

uv run python examples/research/policy_evolution/main.py --output /tmp/meta-evolve-m9

docs.title: Production agent loops
docs.text:
Status: Experimental/live-only. The Meta-Evolve composition below uses shipped local primitives. No production-scale tokenizer run or provider capture is retained in this repository.

Liquid AI's tokenizer-trainer experiment is a useful picture of an evaluated source loop. Two coding agents started from a short outcome-and-constraints specification. Their early implementations passed toy tests, then failed against production data until repeated diagnosis, source changes, and external verification produced a production-grade result. The external harness loaded output with tiktoken and Hugging Face tokenizers, then checked round trips and ID-level agreement. The released toktoktok repository keeps the original AGENTS.md specification.

Meta-Evolve can own the control plane for that shape. It does not provide the coding model, corpus, production machine, or security boundary.

docs.title: Run the miniature first
docs.text:
The credential-free agent_test_repair example exercises the same authority boundary at local scale:

uv run python examples/agents/agent_test_repair/main.py

Its source candidate is an immutable SourceTree. A proposer repairs a private workspace, while an evaluator-owned grader outside the tree decides whether the result passes. Replace the deterministic fixture with a user-owned SDK wrapper to put a live coding agent in the same seat.

docs.title: Scale the same loop
docs.text:
fixed specification + seed SourceTree
                  │
                  ▼
       user-owned coding-agent proposer
                  │
                  ▼
          immutable source candidate
                  │
                  ▼
        evaluator-owned real-data harness
        ├─ build and compatibility checks
        ├─ production-corpus execution
        ├─ peak memory and throughput
        └─ third-party output equivalence
                  │
                  ▼
         metrics + diagnostic evidence
                  │
                  └──────── next bounded trial

The experiment declaration stays small because the provider and production runner remain user-owned adapters:

import meta_evolve as meta

SPECIFICATION = """Build a memory-bounded, multithreaded BPE trainer ..."""


def tokenizer_experiment(build_agent, evaluator, seed):
    budget = meta.Budget(
        evaluations=13,
        trials=12,
        tokens=8_000_000,
        wall_seconds=7 * 24 * 60 * 60,
    )
    task = meta.Task(
        evaluator=evaluator,
        artifact=meta.SourceTree,
        objectives=(meta.Maximize("production_score", satisfy=1.0),),
        budget=budget,
        environment={
            "corpus_digest": "sha256:...",
            "harness_version": "tokenizer-v1",
            "hardware_profile": "epyc-9755-2tb-v1",
        },
    )
    return meta.Experiment(
        task=task,
        seed=seed,
        proposer=build_agent(SPECIFICATION),
        search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=12),
        context=meta.AncestorsOnly(max_records=20, max_chars=32_000),
        experience=meta.PullAccess(
            max_operations=40,
            max_results=40,
            max_records=200,
            max_chars=256_000,
        ),
        random_seed=0,
    )

build_agent owns SDK authentication, tools, session behavior, and provider telemetry. evaluator owns the production runner and returns an EvaluationResult. The corpus digest, harness version, and hardware profile are part of task identity rather than ambient assumptions.

For a live local adapter, retain committed history without promising cold resume:

with meta.Storage.durable("runs/tokenizer") as storage:
    run = meta.run(
        tokenizer_experiment(build_agent, evaluator, seed),
        storage=storage,
        mode="local",
    )

Use durable-local only after every component has a registered reconstruction path and external calls are honestly retry-safe. A paid call or multi-day evaluation repeated after a crash is real work, even when its first result was never committed.

docs.title: Keep reality outside candidate authority
docs.text:
Concern Owner Rust source Candidate artifact Outcome specification Experiment / proposer declaration Production corpus Evaluator environment Compatibility harness Evaluator Model tools and permissions User-owned proposer wrapper Trial and resource ceilings Task and run budgets Which candidate receives work Search policy Whether the result ships User or governance layer

Do not place the hidden harness or mutable production data in the candidate SourceTree. The proposer may receive bounded diagnostics and read-only data access, but it must not be able to edit the judge. The shipped development subprocess is not a security sandbox; use a container, VM, batch worker, or other conforming sandbox provider for a production isolation claim.

docs.title: Give search a useful signal
docs.text:
A final pass/fail check is necessary but weak feedback. A production evaluator can retain separate metrics and evidence while exposing one staged primary score:

Score Observable boundary crossed 0.10 release build succeeds 0.25 toy vocabulary trains 0.40 output loads in both third-party libraries 0.60 token IDs agree on adversarial text 0.80 production shard stays within its memory ceiling 1.00 full production run completes within its declared limits

Candidate defects such as a compiler error or incompatible vocabulary are rankable observations. An unavailable corpus, dead worker, or broken harness is an unrankable typed failure. Never turn infrastructure reliability into a score about the source.

AncestorsOnly supplies selected-lineage feedback. PullAccess lets the agent inspect bounded prior evaluations, exact source occurrences, and canonical source diffs when rejected attempts also matter. Declare the observations used by a proposal in derived_from; that makes “this edit responded to that OOM trace” an auditable causal statement.

Greedy is a good first policy when the staged score reflects progress. If the experiment must continue from the latest source even through temporary regressions, use a small explicit SearchProgram rather than weakening the evaluator to manufacture monotonic scores.

docs.title: Compare agent tracks honestly
docs.text:
Run each model as a separate experiment with the same seed, evaluator, corpus, hardware profile, context and experience grants, and resource limits. Only the proposer declaration should differ. Report both lineages, trials to success, tokens, wall time, failures, and stopping reasons.

Generic Run.compare() deliberately requires the same proposer and seed, so it is not the verdict surface for a model-vs-model experiment. Build a dedicated report that names the model as the treatment. Predeclare an equal stopping rule instead of choosing which arm to stop after seeing intermediate results.

This reproduces the experimental structure, not Liquid AI's historical result. That result also depends on private production data, particular late-2025 model builds, exact tool policies, hardware, and operator decisions. A public replication should begin with a public multilingual/code corpus and a modest machine, then scale only after the evaluator and authority boundary have been tested adversarially.

docs.title: Bound cost
docs.text:
Declare every resource the task permits, then optionally narrow the ceiling for one execution:

task = meta.Task(
    evaluator=grade,
    objectives=(meta.Maximize("quality", satisfy=1.0),),
    budget=meta.Budget(
        evaluations=9,
        trials=8,
        tokens=20_000,
        spend_micros=2_000_000,
        wall_seconds=120,
    ),
)

result = meta.run(
    experiment,
    budget=meta.Budget(trials=3, spend_micros=500_000, wall_seconds=30),
)

A run overlay may narrow but never widen the task budget. satisfy= stops when the primary objective reaches its threshold. Trials and evaluations are coordinator-owned; wrappers report tokens, charged spend, and elapsed time.

spend_micros is integer micro-USD: 1_000_000 means $1.000000. summary(), inspect(), CLI output, and the browser render the same exact committed amount. Estimates belong in evidence, not authoritative usage.

Monetary P1 is Shipped with post-hoc enforcement: once committed usage reaches or exceeds the ceiling, no further work may be authorized. It does not reserve an unknown future provider charge in advance. A wrapper that may have performed paid work but cannot determine exact usage must raise ExecutionAccountingUnknown; recording zero would be false accounting.

Resource exhaustion and unknown accounting are typed unrankable outcomes, not low scores. SDK-side conversion and failed-call rules live in Connect an agent or model.

docs.title: Choose search
docs.text:
Search decides which parent to expand and when to stop; it never evaluates or mutates artifacts itself.

from meta_evolve.policies import Specialists, TreeSearch

greedy = meta.Greedy(max_trials=8)
best_of_n = meta.BestOfN(max_trials=8)
best_of_k = meta.BestOfK(k=3, max_trials=8)
population = meta.Population(size=3, tournament_size=2, max_trials=8)
specialists = Specialists(
    metrics=("case:0", "case:1", "case:2"), max_trials=8
)
tree = TreeSearch(max_trials=8, exploration=2**0.5)

Use Greedy for iterative refinement, BestOfN for independent attempts from the seed, BestOfK for independent fixed-size batches, and Population when temporarily worse branches must remain available. Use Specialists when the evaluator reports the same declared case or slice metrics for every successful candidate and each per-key winner should remain expandable. It is GEPA-style per-key retention, not a Pareto archive; the primary objective's direction applies to every configured metric, exact ties keep the earlier evaluation, extra metrics are ignored, and a missing configured metric is invalid search history. Compare policies only under the same effective task and budget.

Use TreeSearch when improvement may arrive only after expanding a weaker intermediate occurrence. It progressively widens each occurrence, then uses a UCT score whose exploitation term is the globally normalized best successful primary-objective utility in each child subtree. Failed evaluations remain scoreless but selectable through exploration, and all completed successor attempts count as visits. Exact score ties use ascending artifact occurrence ID, so tree selection draws no random stream.

For a small custom parent rule, use the functional facade:

@meta.search(max_trials=4, parent="incumbent")
def refine(search):
    return search.expand(search.incumbent or search.seed)

The configuration is durable and identity-visible. Full custom programs belong in Going further.

docs.title: Evidence companions
docs.text: The searchable policy tour links its raw executed notebook. The comparison chapter links the raw equal-budget report. Neither notebook is a top-level entrance.

docs.title: Use the CLI and browser
docs.text:
An experiment module exposes a side-effect-free experiment() factory. The CLI owns execution and storage:

uv run meta-evolve run examples/operations/command_line/experiment.py --storage ./store
uv run meta-evolve list --storage ./store
uv run meta-evolve inspect <run-id> --storage ./store
uv run meta-evolve resume <run-id> --module examples/operations/command_line/resumable.py --storage ./store
uv run meta-evolve compare <left-id> <right-id> --storage ./store

resume requires a reconstructible durable-local declaration. inspect remains read-only and works for incomplete or unrankable histories.

Install the optional browser dependencies, then serve its loopback UI:

uv sync --extra browser
uv run meta-evolve ui --storage ./store

The browser renders inert stored data and has no execution, resume, promotion, deletion, or remote-control authority. Deployment limits and exact read boundaries live in Browser internals.

docs.title: Give proposals feedback
docs.text:
Pushed feedback is explicit and bounded. AncestorsOnly renders eligible records from causal ancestors into context.bundle:

from meta_evolve.policies import AncestorsOnly

experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=task,
    seed=seed,
    proposer=proposer,
    search=meta.Greedy(max_trials=4),
    context=AncestorsOnly(max_records=10, max_chars=4_000),
)

The proposer can read context.bundle.records or the bounded serialized context.bundle.rendered. It cannot see future results, hidden tests, or records outside the declared policy. A feedback set reused during search is development evidence, not held-out evidence.

Pull access and explicit derivation are advanced authorizations covered in Experience and derivation.

docs.title: Persist and resume
docs.text: Persistence, reopening, and resuming are different jobs. Durable storage records facts; a Run reads them; resume() additionally needs authority to reconstruct the original components.

docs.title: Persist and reopen
docs.text:
with meta.Storage.durable("./run-store") as storage:
    result = meta.run(experiment, storage=storage)

with meta.Storage.read_only("./run-store") as storage:
    reopened = meta.Run(result.id, storage)
    print(reopened.inspect().overview.lifecycle)

Reopening performs no proposal, evaluation, migration, or resume. Custom artifact kinds still need their registered decode authority.

docs.title: Resume durable-local work
docs.text:
Use module-level, deterministic, retry-safe components registered by the experiment factory, then run in mode="durable-local". A later process must load the same declaration and registry before resume() verifies identities and advances only the incomplete recovery frontier.

The shipped factories are:

  • command-line resumable for the concise CLI boundary;
  • crash recovery for deterministic interruption and resume;
  • durable operations for reopening and operational diagnosis.

Resume keeps the original run ID, authority, identities, and effective budgets. It cannot widen limits or reinterpret a committed failure. Replay never calls a proposer, evaluator, context policy, or external provider. See Durability internals for recovery-frontier semantics.

docs.title: Connect an agent or model
docs.text: Status: Shipped. Meta-Evolve owns no model or agent dependency. Keep authentication, sessions, tools, decoding, retries, and provider telemetry in your code, then pass an ordinary callable as the proposer.

docs.title: Return a candidate directly
docs.text:
def propose(parent):
    response = model.generate(
        f"Revise this response while preserving its facts:\n\n{parent}"
    )
    return response.text


result = meta.improve(
    seed=draft,
    proposer=propose,
    evaluator=grade_response,
    trials=3,
)

Provider response objects end at this boundary. The proposer returns the Python candidate understood by the independent evaluator. If a filesystem tool needs cwd, adapt it to return an immutable SourceTree; the canonical code-repair job keeps that integration injectable.

An expanded typed-text job can also receive bounded context:

def propose(parent: meta.Text, context: meta.ProposerContext) -> meta.Text:
    response = model.generate_structured(
        input=str(parent),
        context=context.bundle.rendered,
    )
    return meta.Text(response.candidate)


experiment = meta.Experiment(
    task=meta.Task(evaluator=grade, artifact=meta.Text),
    seed=meta.Text("draft"),
    proposer=propose,
)

docs.title: Return usage and evidence
docs.text:
Use ProposalResult when a wrapper has more to report:

return meta.ProposalResult(
    candidate=response.artifact,
    usage=meta.Usage(
        tokens=response.input_tokens + response.output_tokens,
        spend_micros=response.charged_micros,
        wall_seconds=response.elapsed_seconds,
    ),
    metadata={"model": response.model},
    evidence=(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="sdk-response", data=response.audit),),
)

Model identity, estimated cost, granular token categories, and raw telemetry belong in evidence or metadata. Only an amount the provider actually charged may become shared spend_micros.

docs.title: Record charged spend
docs.text:
A paid call has three honest failure paths:

  1. exact usage is known — return a typed failure carrying that usage;
  2. no paid work started — return a typed failure with zero usage;
  3. paid work may have started but exact usage is unavailable — raise ExecutionAccountingUnknown.

Convert exact provider amounts to integer micro-USD with Decimal, rounding up. Do not multiply a binary float and call ceil: even an exact 0.000123 boundary may become 124 micros.

from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_CEILING, InvalidOperation

from meta_evolve.errors import ExecutionAccountingUnknown


def charged_micros(cost_usd: object) -> int:
    """Exact micro-USD, rounded up, or refuse to guess."""

    try:
        amount = (
            cost_usd
            if isinstance(cost_usd, Decimal)
            else Decimal(str(cost_usd))
        )
    except (InvalidOperation, ValueError, TypeError) as error:
        raise ExecutionAccountingUnknown(
            f"unreadable charge {cost_usd!r}"
        ) from error
    if not amount.is_finite() or amount < 0:
        raise ExecutionAccountingUnknown(f"invalid charge {amount}")
    return int(
        (amount * 1_000_000).to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_CEILING)
    )

Decode the provider body with parse_float=Decimal when possible; a float has already discarded digits and cannot be repaired. Never raise an ordinary exception after billing or return a bare failure without usage, because either would falsely record zero. Trial and evaluation counts remain coordinator-owned.

docs.title: Authority and reproducibility
docs.text:
The wrapper may propose candidate content. It cannot choose the evaluator, change budgets, grant itself experience, edit audit history, or promote a result. Committed requests, evidence, usage, failures, and artifacts support inspection and replay; Meta-Evolve does not claim a later external call will regenerate byte-identical output.

Start with the credential-free user-owned SDK example. For migration rules, read SDK migration. For staged production evaluation, authority, and honest replication limits, read Production agent loops.

docs.title: Write an evaluator
docs.text:
An evaluator receives a decoded candidate and independently returns one of three supported score shapes:

def scalar(candidate):
    return 0.75

def mapping(candidate):
    return {"quality": 0.75, "length": len(candidate)}

def rich(candidate):
    return meta.EvaluationResult(
        metrics={"quality": 0.75},
        evidence=(meta.EvidenceDraft(kind="checks/v1", data={"passed": 3}),),
        usage=meta.Usage(tokens=120),
    )

A scalar maps to the task's primary metric. A mapping records every declared metric. EvaluationResult additionally carries uncertainty, evidence, usage, or a typed failure. Return poor scores for valid but poor work. Return a typed failure for output that cannot be judged, or let an unexpected exception be recorded as evaluator failure.

The task's first objective alone controls default ranking and stopping. Use run.best("metric") or run.best_trial("metric") to query another declared objective. For hard checks and held-out grading, see Grade with checks and rubrics.

docs.title: Write a proposer
docs.text:
Return a Python candidate directly unless the tool requires cwd. The smallest proposer accepts a parent and returns one successor:

def revise(parent):
    return parent + " One concrete next action."

Accept context when the proposal needs recorded randomness, the logical step, declared objectives, pushed records, or authorized experience:

def revise(parent, context):
    choice = context.rng.choice(("today", "within one business day"))
    return f"{parent} I will act {choice}."

Do not let the proposer grade, expand its budget, promote itself, or read hidden evaluator state. Raise an exception only for a proposer fault; return a candidate for valid work even when you expect it to score poorly.

When a filesystem tool requires cwd, wrap that callback in the root-level meta.WorkspaceProposer; see Repair code with an agent.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
The canonical agent_test_repair job gives a proposer buggy source and a failing case. An evaluator-owned subprocess—not the candidate or agent—decides whether the captured successor passes.

"""An injected proposer repairs a real bug; a grader subprocess decides.

The seed is a ``SourceTree`` holding a function whose documented contract and
shipped behaviour disagree on one character. The proposer is supplied by the
caller through the user-owned callable boundary: the committed script injects
a deterministic fixture, and a real SDK wrapper plugs into the same seam. The
evaluator is a *separate process* running an evaluator-owned grader the
proposer never sees, so the score is a verdict about the code rather than a
